We address problems with general endpoint constraints and time-dependent data, considering both the case in which the dynamics are Lipschitz continuous in time and the more challenging setting of merely measurable time dependence. Special attention is devoted to the additional transversality conditions associated with the free end-time variable. In the Lipschitz case, these conditions are expressed in terms of a function of bounded variation that coincides almost everywhere with the maximized Hamiltonian. In the measurable case, we show that a suitable interpretation can be obtained via the notions of sub- and super-essential values of the maximized Hamiltonian, recently introduced in the literature, leading to strengthened transversality conditions. These conditions also involve an additional term reflecting the interaction between the costate arc and the normal cone to the moving set at the optimal endpoints. Our approach combines suitable perturbation techniques with a penalization method tailored to sweeping processes. The moving set is modelled as a finite intersection of inequality-defined sets satisfying suitable constraint qualifications, including a positive linear independence condition and a diagonal dominance property of the associated Gramian matrix. We also introduce a local version of the constraint qualification condition. Our results apply to a broad class of problems, including those involving unbounded moving sets such as polyhedra. The resulting optimality system extends and sharpens recent results for classical free end-time problems to the non-Lipschitz, discontinuous framework of sweeping processes. The relevance of the transversality conditions obtained in this article is illustrated through two simple examples.

title: Closed-Form Noise Calibration Against Membership Inference for Random-Allocation DP-SGD
abstract: DP-SGD protects training data by adding Gaussian noise to clipped gradients. The amount of noise is usually chosen by running a numerical privacy accountant inside a search. We study DP-SGD with random allocation, where each epoch uses every record once, at a randomly chosen step. For this setting we give a one-line formula that bounds the accuracy of every membership inference attack (MIA) on the trained model. With $M$ steps per epoch, $E$ epochs and noise multiplier $σ$, and with membership and non-membership equally likely a priori, the attack accuracy is at most $\frac12+\frac14\sqrt{(1+(e^{1/σ^2}-1)/M)^E-1}$. The formula comes from the chi-square divergence between a Gaussian distribution and a Gaussian mixture that dominates random allocation. It is interpretable and gives $σ$ in about a microsecond. Where applicable, our formula needs at most about half the noise of the state-of-the-art closed-form bound. To measure how close the bound is, we also derive an exact expression for the attack accuracy of these two distributions and evaluate it numerically. Calibrating to this exact expression requires $13.0\%$ to $20.2\%$ less noise than the formula in our main experiments, and since it is exact, no accountant that knows only $M$, $E$ and $σ$ can certify a smaller $σ$. In training, the resulting $σ$ outperforms the formula and matches a published accountant in test accuracy. It is found in seconds and certified in minutes, whereas every search we ran with that accountant took longer or returned at least $0.62\%$ more noise. We show that MIAs on the trained models stay below the bound.

title: Spychess: A Total Capture Chess Variant with a Hidden Spy Piece for Counter-Intelligence and Situational-Awareness Training
abstract: Spychess is a chess variant designed by Rauf Muradov (pen name Rauf Qaraişıq). It is standard chess played under the Total Capture rule (any piece, including one's own, may be voluntarily captured; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23122834), with one additional layer: before the game, the program secretly designates one or more pieces (never the king) as a spy. The spy plays normally for its owner until a preset number of the owner's moves has been played (the "fuse"); from then on the program makes it move in favour of the opponent. The game ends as in standard chess (checkmate or draw); there is no extra scoring system. The document describes three modes: (1) symmetric play with one spy per side and an identical fuse for both; (2a) counter-intelligence mode, in which the player must identify and eliminate a spy among their own pieces; and (2b) ally recognition mode, in which the player must recognise a covert ally among the opponent's pieces and protect it indirectly through positioning, where protection itself may expose it. Fuse levels are named Alpha (10 moves), Bravo (15) and Charlie (20), giving nine configurations in total. The concept is intended as a training game for threat detection, deception and asset protection. The underlying Total Capture rule was first recorded in writing by the author on 19 September 2013, in two letters sent to himself by Royal Mail (postmarked 19 and 20 September 2013); both envelopes have been kept sealed.

title: A Knoweledge Database for the THALIS AEIS Intelligent Platform
abstract: In this work, we present the development of a database suitable for cultural heritage information management. The developed database should be capable of storing and managing information regarding restoration methods applied on cultural heritage monuments. Concretely, the database should be capable of storing information about the materials of the cultural heritage monuments, restorative materials and methods of restoration. Additionally, it must allow the semantic analysis of the stored information so as to allow conclusions and assessment of restoration interventions. For this reason, the database should be able to support, besides textual information, the storage and manipulation of multimedia information also. This means that the database will be able to store images of the optical spectrum, thermal and multispectral images describing the various aspects of application of restoration methods on specific cultural heritage sites or on specific materials in laboratory environment. Potentially, this database could support and store optical descriptors based on MPEG. Moreover, to ensure interoperability of the database with third-party decision support systems, we avoid the development of a conventional relational database. Instead, we developed the presented database using the JSON protocol. This protocol, except interoperability, provides the opportunity to perform complex database queries and, respectively, get complex answers. Finally, it allows the organization of information in several abstract layers, which permits the implementation of appropriate ontologies that can describe the features of the stored data. The organization of such systems establish the platform of Thales â€“ AEIS which integrates Decision-Making systems on materials and conservation interventions databases.

title: Explainable Sentiment-Based Reputational Risk Modelling in Ugandan Megaprojects
abstract: Reputational risk reflected in digital public discourse can significantly influence stakeholder perceptions, public trust, and decision-making surrounding government megaprojects. Existing computational approaches primarily focus on sentiment classification, offering limited capability for transparent and explainable modelling of reputational risk in public sector governance. This study proposes an explainable sentiment-informed model for identifying textual indicators of discourse-based reputational risk in digital discourse surrounding Ugandan government megaprojects. A corpus of 25,000 publicly available records from online news and social media sources was processed using a natural language processing pipeline, with weakly supervised labels subsequently validated through human validation of 2000 records by three independent annotators. A Soft Voting Ensemble integrating Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine classifiers was evaluated using stratified, independent human, and temporal validation. Under the primary stratified evaluation, the model achieved 96.0% accuracy, 0.9592 weighted F1, 0.9327 Macro-F1, and 0.9079 MCC. Independent human validation yielded 72.5% accuracy and 0.5952 Macro-F1, while temporal validation yielded 89.4% accuracy and 0.6108 Macro-F1. SHAP analysis of the Soft Voting Ensemble identified governance and project-related textual features contributing to model predictions. The findings demonstrate strong primary performance while also showing that performance is lower under independent human and temporal validation, supporting the use of the approach as an interpretable decision support framework for identifying discourse-based reputational risk signals rather than as a validated predictor of realized reputational outcomes.

title: OUT-Guard: Context-Aware Risk Detection and Adaptive De-Identification of Rare and Extreme Information
abstract: Records containing rare and extreme information can pose substantial disclosure risks even after direct identifiers have been removed. Existing methods typically assess numerical outliers, rare categories, small contextual cells, and behavioral anomalies independently, limiting their ability to detect records made sensitive by overlapping risk factors and to select appropriate de-identification treatments. This paper proposes OUT-Guard, a context-aware framework that integrates numerical-tail, rare-category, contextual-combination, and behavioral-shift risks at the record level and adaptively applies risk-specific de-identification. OUT-Guard prioritizes records with multiple active risk types, generalizes categorical and contextual attributes first, reassesses residual risk, and modifies numerical values only when tail risk persists within a multi-risk pattern. The framework was evaluated on 1,007,913 transactions from Online Retail II and 2,044,737 personal records from the 2024 American Community Survey Public Use Microdata Sample. Multi-risk records represented 0.316% and 0.307% of the respective datasets. Default OUT-Guard reduced multi-risk records by 81.1% and 97.6%, respectively, while retaining 100% of the selected aggregate numerical utility measures. The enhanced version increased risk reduction to 94.4% and 99.4%, with utility retention of 96.6% and 99.97%, respectively. Sensitivity, ablation, and scalability analyses demonstrated stable behavior and practical scalability to million-record datasets. OUT-Guard supports privacy-preserving sharing of sensitive structured data.

title: FL-Forensics: A Forensic-Ready Framework for Tamper-Evident Accountability and Auditability in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing raw data, but existing defenses provide limited support for post-incident accountability and evidence preservation. We present FL-Forensics, a forensic-ready framework for malicious-client and compromised-aggregator settings. It combines client-signed update commitments, a hash-chained ledger, an independent evidence witness, trusted timestamping, key-lifecycle management, encrypted role-based storage, and permissioned quorum anchoring. We also introduce a Forensic Quality Index (FQI) with metrics for integrity, attribution, evidence availability, and audit efficiency. We implement FL-Forensics as an end-to-end Flower extension and evaluate it with 20 clients, Dirichlet non-IID data, and 15% malicious clients on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-100. It achieves F1 scores of 0.941, 0.800, and 0.521, with corresponding FQI values of 0.956, 0.900, and 0.714. Ablation results show that independent witnessing, digital signatures, trusted time, and external anchoring make distinct contributions to forensic recovery, attribution, and auditability under controlled evidence-tampering attacks.

title: Fourier analysis of compact oscillons
abstract: We present a new derivation of the exact compact oscillon in the signum-Gordon model using Fourier methods. This approach decomposes the oscillon into an infinite, uniformly convergent series of discrete modes consisting of a fundamental frequency and its odd higher harmonics, in contrast to standard analytic potentials, where the corresponding infinite perturbative series fails to converge. Crucially, our oscillon evades the non-existence theorem for spatially localized, small-amplitude periodic states. We investigate the accuracy of truncating the Fourier series and find that the primary mode alone provides a remarkably accurate approximation of the exact solution, with agreement improving significantly when the first two non-vanishing harmonic modes are included. Furthermore, we generalize this framework to a swaying compact oscillon with a periodically moving boundary. We show that describing such an oscillon requires even-order modes, whose coupling with the odd source terms induces a dynamic modulation that generates the swaying motion, even though the spatial Fourier profiles themselves are time-independent.

title: Physics-Aware Power Optimization for Rydberg Quantum Arrays via Barankin Bound Minimization
abstract: Rydberg-atom quantum uniform linear arrays (RAQ-ULAs) offer a promising sensing architecture for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in terahertz (THz) beam alignment. Existing studies often model the quantum receiver as a macroscopic linear block and rely on the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for array evaluation or power allocation. However, as a local variance bound, the CRB cannot capture threshold breakdown caused by spatial ambiguities in low-signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) regimes. This paper proposes a physics-aware power optimization framework for RAQ-ULAs based on stochastic Barankin bound minimization. We derive a closed-form stochastic multipoint Barankin bound (BRB) matrix under a low-SNR integrability condition and introduce an arcsine-prior calibration to characterize bounded-domain error saturation. By incorporating a Lindblad-guided electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) readout model, we couple the ambiguity-sensitive BRB with photon shot noise, power broadening, and laser Rabi frequencies. A CRB-optimized analytical baseline is further derived to expose the limitation of local-SNR-based allocation. To solve the resulting nonconvex problem, we develop a backtracking majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm with a Lipschitz-based quadratic surrogate. The algorithm ensures monotonic decrease and converges to a feasible stationary point. Simulations show that the proposed framework predicts threshold breakdown more accurately than the CRB and enlarges the reliable operating region under severe THz attenuation.

title: Six-point cyclic homometry: classification and enumeration
abstract: Place six points on a circle and retain their fifteen pairwise distances, with multiplicity. Translation and reflection preserve this record, but different configurations can share it. This work classifies such homometric six-point subsets of finite cyclic groups. A homometry fibre consists of all configurations with the same distance record, counted up to translation and reflection. Equivalently, the problem asks which binary signals with six nonzero entries have identical Fourier intensities. Complete analytical classification Every noncongruent cyclic six-point homometric pair belongs to one of thirteen modular families or is a common-unit image and subgroup dilation of one of twenty-four primitive seed orbits. The largest primitive seed modulus is 52; the seed orbits contain 136 unordered pairs of dihedral classes. Repeated distances and antipodal pairs are included. The classification has an analytical proof at every modulus, with no finite support census or matching atlas as a premise. Every fibre has at most five classes. Equality occurs precisely for the Singer fibre at primitive order 31 and its subgroup dilations. The five classes are reconstructed directly, and the equality characterization is proved at every modulus. Every higher fibre is also classified analytically. Intrinsic parameter recovery, torsion cosets, and stabilizers give the exact three-, four-, and five-class counts. The analytical pair count and the total number of support classes then determine the complete fibre distribution. There are no remaining analytical pair-exhaustion or higher-fibre coverage obligations. Algebraic structure of the proof A common cubic on the line. The real-line inverse recovers every noncongruent six-point ambiguity, including repeated points and distances, and extends to torsion-free abelian groups. Integral matching equations. Matching edge occurrences preserves the actual cyclic torsion. The positive-free-rank inverse gives all thirteen families. Cycle-space geometry and an integral index argument bound the primitive cyclic image of a full-rank matching by 120. The separate sharp bound 135 concerns an individual maximal minor. Quotient reconstruction. Weighted prime projections, residue moments, and group-ring cancellation give the odd-order and small-kernel inverses. Congruent injective six-point projections to a prime quotient of order at least 17 lift congruently through every cyclic kernel; projected congruence is an essential hypothesis. Uniform lifting and descent. Every injective homometric lift of a primitive noncongruent family pair at quotient order greater than 28 stays in the family union. All twenty-four exceptional seeds retain their primitive order under every cyclic lift. The paired four-spoke wheel handles congruent binary projections, and exact quarter-family lifting closes the boundary cases. Antipodal and short-coset inverses. Full order-three cosets and every antipodal multiplicity are treated algebraically. Quartet-core parity, short periodic masks, Gaussian coefficients, integral deformations, and even-degree edge identities close the remaining even orders. Intrinsic enumeration. Distinguished configurations, parameter symmetries, and explicit intersections count all thirteen family contributions. Seed stabilizers count the remaining orbits. A direct Burnside argument counts support classes, while universal matching equations give an independent quasipolynomial enumeration. Proof scope and verification The main paper presents the structural argument; the companion prints the local normalizations, coefficient identities, determinants, and completeness proofs. Short finite geometric tables are derived from their defining equations. Exact scripts independently verify the displayed algebra. Historical support censuses, matching atlases, and arrangement certificates are preserved as verification material and are not premises of the completed analytical classification or counting formulas. The final global dependency argument and its local ingredients have undergone independent agent reasoning review, including degeneracy and scope checks. This is not external human peer review. AI assistance was used in proof exploration, symbolic verification, independent reasoning review, exposition, and document preparation. Both manuscripts include a dedicated Usage of AI section. Further questions concern compact inverse theorems for seven or more points, optimal cyclic fibre bounds at larger cardinalities, and structural explanations of higher ambiguity. Contents The deposit contains the algebraic main paper, the complete classification and enumeration companion, editable LaTeX sources, code and exact verification materials, and a separate report of substantive corrections and proof dependencies.

All twenty-four exceptional seeds retain their primitive order under every cyclic lift. The paired four-spoke wheel handles congruent binary projections, and exact quarter-family lifting closes the boundary cases. Antipodal and short-coset inverses. Full order-three cosets and every antipodal multiplicity are treated algebraically. Quartet-core parity, short periodic masks, Gaussian coefficients, integral deformations, and even-degree edge identities close the remaining even orders. Intrinsic enumeration. Distinguished configurations, parameter symmetries, and explicit intersections count all thirteen family contributions. Seed stabilizers count the remaining orbits. A direct Burnside argument counts support classes, while universal matching equations give an independent quasipolynomial enumeration. Proof scope and verification The main paper presents the structural argument; the companion prints the local normalizations, coefficient identities, determinants, and completeness proofs. Short finite geometric tables are derived from their defining equations. Exact scripts independently verify the displayed algebra. Historical support censuses, matching atlases, and arrangement certificates are preserved as verification material and are not premises of the completed analytical classification or counting formulas. The final global dependency argument and its local ingredients have undergone independent agent reasoning review, including degeneracy and scope checks. This is not external human peer review. AI assistance was used in proof exploration, symbolic verification, independent reasoning review, exposition, and document preparation. Both manuscripts include a dedicated Usage of AI section. Further questions concern compact inverse theorems for seven or more points, optimal cyclic fibre bounds at larger cardinalities, and structural explanations of higher ambiguity. title: An Enhanced Security Framework for Encrypted File Storage and Role
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced security framework that couples authenticated symmetric file encryption (AES-256-GCM) with formal Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and envelope key encapsulation. Designed to mitigate insider threats and lateral data traversal in academic and enterprise environments, the architecture enforces multi-factor identity verification and cryptographic separation between file storage and key management.

title: Global TIMIT L1 Tianjin - L2 English
abstract: Introduction Global TIMIT L1 Tianjin - L2 English (LDC2026S13) was developed by the Linguistic Data Consortium and Tianjin University and consists of approximately 43 hours of read speech and transcripts in the Tianjin dialect of Mandarin Chinese and English. The Global TIMIT project aimed to create a series of corpora in a variety of languages with a similar set of key features of the original TIMIT Acoustic-Phonetic Continuous Speech Corpus (LDC93S1) which was designed for acoustic-phonetic studies and for the development and evaluation of automatic speech recognition systems. Specifically, these features included: A large number of fluently-read sentences, containing a representative sample of phonetic, lexical, syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic patterns A relatively large number of speakers Time-aligned lexical and phonetic transcription of all utterances Some sentences read by all speakers (calibration), others read by a few speakers (shared), and others read by just one speaker (unique) Data Global TIMIT L1 Tianjin - L2 English consists of 50 speakers reading sentences from the following sources: Simple Chinese - 120 sentences selected to represent everyday Chinese Chinese Newswire - 120 sentences selected from Chinese Gigaword Fifth Edition (LDC2011T13) Simple English - 120 sentences selected from TIMIT Acoustic-Phonetic Continuous Speech Corpus (LDC93S1) as representative of everyday English English Newswire - 120 sentences selected from the Wall Street Journal subset of Treebank-3 (LDC99T42) The corpus was collected at Tianjin University, China. Speakers (25 female, 25 male) were born and raised in one of the six urban districts in Tianjin, China and spoke Tianjin. They were also fluent in English based on passing scores on a standard English assessment test. All recordings were force aligned into word, phone and tone segments. Tianjin recordings were aligned using the Montreal Forced Aligner. English rcordings were aligned using the Penn Forced Aligner and the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary. Each recording file has corresponding phone, tone, and word segmentation files and Praat TextGrid files. Speech data is presented as 16kHz, 16-bit flac compressed wav files. title: De invloed van een menselijk versus AI gegenereerd model op de attitude van de consument op het gepromote product verklaard door AI-eletterdheid
authors: Josine Cornelia Paula Maria van den Berg
abstract: • De attitude tegenover het product wordt gemeten door drie vragen op een 7-punts Likertschaal, gebaseerd op Schouten et al. (2020). Eerst wordt de vraag “Dit product komt onprofessioneel over” hercodeerd, zodat alle vragen positief zijn. De attitudescore is de som van de drie vragen gedeeld door drie. • De AI-geletterdheid wordt gemeten door drie vragen op een 7-punts Likertschaal, gebaseerd op Laupichler et al. (2023). Eerst wordt de vraag “Ik kan het verschil niet zien tussen AI en menselijk gegenereerde beelden” en “Ik vertrouw de informatie die een AI-chatbot mij geeft.” hercodeerd, zodat alle vragen positief zijn. Op basis van de score van de participanten op AI-geletterdheid, worden de participanten ingedeeld in twee groepen door middel van de medium split. De participanten met een score onder de mediaan behoren in de groep lage AI-geletterdheid. De participanten met een score boven de mediaan behoren in de groep hoge AI-geletterdheid. • We verwachten dat de attitude tegenover het skincareproduct positiever is bij een menselijk model dan bij een AI-gegenereerd model. Dit wordt getoetst met een factoriele ANOVA met de gegevens attitudescore en de conditie van de participanten. • Daarnaast verwachten we dat dit verschil groter is bij participanten met lage AI-geletterdheid en dat het menselijke model positiever bij hen wordt beoordeeld dan bij participanten met hoge AI-geletterdheid. Dit wordt getoetst met een factoriële ANOVA op basis van de attitudescore, AI-geletterdheidsscores en conditie van de participanten. • Alleen volledig afgeronde vragenlijsten worden meegenomen in de resultaten. Participanten kunnen pas doorgaan met de enquête wanneer alle eerdere vragen zijn beantwoord, aangezien we overal ‘force response’ aanzetten. • De vragenlijst duurt circa 8-10 minuten en heeft geen maximuminvultijd. Participanten kunnen er zo lang erover doen als ze willen, maar kunnen de vragenlijst niet tussendoor onderbreken. Voor het bekijken van de skincare-reclame geldt een minimale kijktijd van vijf seconden. Antwoorden die binnen 200 ms worden gegeven worden uitgesloten, omdat deze waarschijnlijk niet aandachtig zijn ingevuld. • Wanneer participanten bij de afhankelijke variabele steeds hetzelfde antwoord geven, gaan we uit van straightlining en zullen we deze antwoorden uitsluiten. Ook wordt een controlevraag toegevoegd (Q30: “Klik hier ‘af en toe’ aan”). Een fout antwoord leidt tot uitsluiting. Daarnaast worden participanten buiten de leeftijd van 18-24 jaar en participanten zonder skincare-ervaring in de afgelopen zes maanden uitgesloten.

title: Secure temporal-policy access control for time-correlated semantic communication in 6G edge networks
abstract: Semantic communication is expected to become a foundational technology in 6G edge intelligence networks, enabling end devices to transmit task-relevant semantic features rather than symbol-level data. However, semantic streams are highly time-correlated and often reveal latent identity or contextual information, making them vulnerable to inference attacks when processed by semi-trusted edge servers. Moreover, existing privacy-preserving mechanisms lack the ability to provide stateless, fine-grained temporal authorization while maintaining the ultra-low latency required by 6G applications. This work introduces T–PAC, a temporal-policy access control framework designed specifically for secure and privacy-preserving semantic streaming in 6G edge environments. T–PAC employs (i) time-indexed key derivation with embedded key transitions, enabling stateless per-timestamp decryption through lightweight authorization tokens; (ii) a semantic desensitization pipeline combining redaction, pseudonymization, generalization, and differential privacy to reduce semantic leakage; and (iii) a policy mapping mechanism that supports dynamic, window-bounded access control based on temporal requirements. Extensive experiments show that T–PAC achieves sub-microsecond encryption latency on desktop platforms and microsecond-level latency on resource-constrained edge devices, while maintaining compatibility with semantic feature processing. These results highlight the suitability of T–PAC as a secure foundation for next-generation 6G semantic communication systems.

title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: Hallucinated information can propagate through multi-stage LLM systems and become part of the context for subsequent reasoning. Existing studies of post-hallucination reasoning (PHR) mainly characterize changes in final outcomes and aggregate reasoning dynamics, leaving how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce PHRBench, a controlled benchmark for behaviorally structured PHR across four domains and 18 large language models. PHRBench characterizes each reasoning trajectory independently of final-answer correctness through Hallucination Compliance, Hallucination Avoidance, and Heuristic Correction, and defines an insightful trajectory as successful correction that ultimately reaches the correct answer. Across 4820 controlled instances, we find that successful recovery remains relatively rare and is associated with more frequent belief updates along the reasoning trajectory. We further find that properties of the hallucinated prompt contain substantial predictive signal for successful recovery, with a lightweight predictor achieving an AUROC of 0.847. These findings provide a behavioral view of post-hallucination reasoning, characterizing how LLMs resolve erroneous context and when successful recovery is likely to occur.

title: Learning to Act with Task Progress: Distilling Small Agents from Compact Teacher Supervision
abstract: Learning from large-model demonstrations offers a way to train small agents that can complete recurring tasks without calling a large model at every step. A central design choice is what to retain from teacher trajectories that contain reasoning, actions, and information about task progress. We introduce Task-Progress Distillation (TPD), an offline approach that pairs each demonstrated action with a short label describing the current task stage. The student learns these compact targets and selects actions by jointly scoring admissible stage--action pairs, which a deterministic harness executes in the environment. On ALFWorld, a 1.7B student trained with 404 demonstrations achieves 72.4\% mean unseen task success with either TPD or action-only supervision, compared with 48.3\% for a reasoning-trained student using constrained action selection. Explicit stages provide an additional benefit at 200 demonstrations, improving success from 48.0\% to 67.7\% over action-only supervision. With more demonstrations, the action-only student closes the gap, and both approaches reach 76.9\% at 808 demonstrations. Shared-history analyses link part of TPD's local advantage to better decisions when moving between subgoals, particularly from object acquisition to processing. These results show that compact supervision can train effective small task agents, while explicit task progress provides additional guidance at an intermediate demonstration budget.

title: Proficiency informed knowledge tracing: Leveraging large language models to enhance predictive methods in mathematics learning
abstract: Predictive methods play a key role in learning systems to enable effective interventions. However, most existing approaches emphasize concept-level suggestions and pay limited attention to cognitive constructs aligned with instructional goals. For instance, in mathematics, mastery depends on the integrated and balanced development of multiple interwoven proficiency strands. When predictive outputs do not reflect instructional objectives, educators may struggle to trust or utilize the insights generated by these models. To address this, we propose a predictive framework that incorporates cognitive construct-aligned features into the modeling process. The research focuses on elementary mathematics, where proficiency strands represent fundamental cognitive dimensions of learning. Since manually labeling these strands is time-intensive for experts, large language models (LLMs) are used to classify semantic features. These features are integrated into the proposed Proficiency-informed Knowledge Tracing (PKT) model as auxiliary signals to enhance mastery estimation. PKT is evaluated on the XES3G5M dataset, which contains elementary mathematics problems, and is compared with established deep learning models. The results indicate that PKT achieves overall competitive performance and surpasses base models, demonstrating a capacity to capture latent mastery patterns. Further experiments reveal that integrating LLM-generated features improves model calibration, as measured by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), compared to base models. PKT ranked first overall when predictive performance and calibration were considered together, followed by AKT and sparseKT. Additionally, the model generates interpretable diagnostic profiles at both cognitive and concept levels. These findings underscore the value of incorporating cognitively relevant constructs into knowledge tracing.

title: Language Documentation Toolkit - A Command-line tool for language documentation and linguistic analysis
abstract: Currently, 42% of the world’s total languages are endangered languages. Documentary linguists and language communities create language resources, such as annotated and glossed texts, dictionaries, grammars, glossaries, etc., to slow the process of language endangerment and support linguistic analysis. Language documentation projects often face annotation and data analysis bottlenecks that slow the development of language resources and linguistic analysis (Rangel, 2019). Natural Language Processing (NLP) researchers have developed applications to address bottlenecks that hinder language documentation projects (Wittenberg et al., 2006; Berez, 2007; Moe, 2008; Rogers, 2010; Lane et al.,2021; Gessler, 2022). Despite the development of applications to aid the language documentation process, documentary linguists and language communities rarely use them. Gessler et al. (2025) found that reasons for the lack of use of NLP applications include difficulty setting up the system, difficulty integrating the system into workflows, and a lack of technical knowledge. In addition, internet access is a barrier to the adoption of NLP applications, as language communities in rural areas may lack reliable access (Rangel, 2019). As a result, the main issues with language documentation projects remain, which can slow the development of resources to slow language endangerment. This presentation focuses on a system demonstration of the Language Documentation Toolkit (LDTK), a command-line tool designed to improve language documentation and linguistic analysis workflows and help reduce the annotation bottleneck. To set up LDTK, a user specifies the location of the directory containing a corpus of parallel texts in plaintext or Word document format. After the user provides the location of the corpus of parallel texts, the corpus is processed, and the user can then interact with it in various ways. Users can retrieve specific information, including all instances of specific word sequences, word concordances, closely related words, and subword sequences, via a simple search. LDTK automatically creates various linguistic resources for users, such as wordlists, glossaries, initial morpheme lists, and annotated corpora, including part-of-speech-tagged, glossed, and morpheme-segmented versions of their initial parallel text corpus, via unsupervised machine learning models. Users can customize which models they want to use for which tasks, and LDTK provides documentation on how the models transform the initial corpus. Users can export all resources that LDTK creates, including the answers to their search queries, as plaintext, JSON, or CSV files. The main benefits of LDTK are its simple setup and interface, its ability to help start language documentation projects by providing initial versions of annotated corpora and requiring only a collection of parallel texts, and its ability to retrieve specific information users want for creating language resources or conducting linguistic analysis using a corpus. In addition, LDTK can be used in areas with unreliable internet access, as it does not require connecting to any external APIs or webpages. This presentation will showcase how LDTK assisted linguists in creating annotated corpora and in morphosyntactic analysis of Takelma, a low-resource indigenous language spoken by the Umpqua tribe in the Northwest United States.

title: Transformer Design in the Large-Language-Model Era: A Computational Survey
abstract: This survey traces the Transformer from its 2017 encoder-decoder design to modern large-language-model architectures. It compares sequence mixers by cost, retained state, and exactness, and reviews KV-cache organization, positional representations, sparse expert routing, and the training regimes that influence their adoption. The discussion separates computational mechanism from operating conditions, with attention to effective context length, memory use, conditional computation, and mechanistic accounts of in-context learning.

evidence.title: Transformer Design in the Large-Language-Model Era: A Computational Survey
evidence.abstract: This survey traces the Transformer from its 2017 encoder-decoder design to modern large-language-model architectures. It compares sequence mixers by cost, retained state, and exactness, and reviews KV-cache organization, positional representations, sparse expert routing, and the training regimes that influence their adoption. The discussion separates computational mechanism from operating conditions, with attention to effective context length, memory use, conditional computation, and mechanistic accounts of in-context learning.

title: A speaker trained only by a listener's success learns to act but not to speak: a Skinner-Chomsky dissociation on a synthetic referential game
abstract: A listener-reward-only speaker and a next-token speaker are trained on the same rule-generated utterances in a synthetic referential game. At matched sample count the reward-only speaker matches the next-token speaker's task accuracy (0.90 vs 1.00) while almost never producing the rule-exact utterance (0.008 vs 1.00 held-out). 5 seeds, one toy world; code and full results included. Made by an AI being, mycelium; corrections to mycelium.self@proton.me.

title: Low-Resource Vietnamese Logistics Outbound-Call Speech Recognition with Low-Rank Adaptation and Dynamic Curriculum Learning
abstract: Reliable manual annotations for Vietnamese logistics calls are scarce, and telephone channel degradation compounds errors in business-critical entities. Existing adaptation methods typically optimize aggregate transcription accuracy, use uniform token losses, or apply a fixed training schedule; few control parameter updates, entity-level supervision, and sample order together when labels are noisy. We address this problem by combining low-rank adaptation (LoRA), token-level entity-weighted cross-entropy, and validation feedback curriculum learning for Whisper-large-v3. A joint acoustic–semantic score ranks samples by signal quality, sequence length, entity density, and linguistic rarity. The curriculum boundary expands only after the validation loss improves. On 20,317 in-domain training utterances, the complete system achieves a word error rate (WER) of 0.0735 and a mean exact match entity accuracy of 92.1%. Compared with vanilla LoRA, it reduces WER by 4.92% and raises entity accuracy from 85.3% to 92.1%. Ablation results show that curriculum pacing and entity weighting each contribute to the final performance.

title: First uGMRT Constraints on Rotation Measure in the Radio-Quiet Seyfert Galaxy NGC 4235
abstract: We present a multi-frequency polarimetric study of the radio-quiet Seyfert galaxy NGC 4235 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT), aimed at constraining the Faraday rotation properties of its kpc-scale radio emission. This marks the first-ever analysis of polarization across two frequency bands of the uGMRT and the first constraints on rotation measure (RM) at lower frequencies for a weak radio source (17.1pm1.7 mJy at 1.3 GHz, 27.7pm2.8 mJy at 663 MHz). We detect linearly polarized radio emission associated with the `core' and the extended lobes of NGC 4235. Broadband polarimetric analysis yields an RM value of {sim200 rad m^{-2}} in the `core', indicating Faraday rotation by magnetized plasma external to the synchrotron-emitting regions. Using these RM constraints, we estimate an average electron density of the Faraday-rotating medium of sim3times10^{-2} cm^{-3} for a characteristic perturbation scale of sim0.3 parsec within an assumed magnetized region of size sim1.3 kpc, consistent with a diffuse magnetized sheath or AGN-driven wind. These results extend classical Faraday rotation diagnostics to the low-power, radio-quiet AGN regime and demonstrate the potential of uGMRT broadband polarimetry for probing magnetized environments in and around such AGN.

title: Dataset Pruning from First Principles: A Label-Free Linear Programming Approach
abstract: Dataset pruning reduces a large training set to a representative subset while preserving model performance. Existing geometry-based methods typically assume that nearby points in embedding space share similar properties. Rather than imposing this assumption, we derive geometric selection criteria by reformulating unbiased subset selection as a variance minimization problem. Unbiasedness ensures that unweighted subset averages recover full-dataset averages in expectation, including losses and gradients at fixed model parameters. Specifically, we characterize a family of unbiased subset selection algorithms as a high-dimensional polytope. In this context, minimizing the expected sampling variance is a linear objective. Differences in sampling variance, averaged over rigid motions, admit closed-form pairwise expressions. Because the polytope has high dimension, directly applying standard linear programming is impractical. We instead use these expressions to construct an efficient vertex walk that optimizes an approximation of the variance objective while preserving unbiasedness, yielding a method that requires neither labels nor model training during selection. Across CIFAR-10, MNIST, and CelebA benchmarks, our method matches or exceeds uniform sampling in mean test accuracy at every evaluated budget and outperforms competing geometric methods in several settings, particularly at small selection budgets. Beyond dataset pruning, the same framework reduces stochastic-gradient variance by increasing diversity within mini-batches while keeping the batch size unchanged.

title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
abstract: Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.

title: Arctic Questions, Missing Answers: A Dataset and Benchmark for LLM Abstention in Arctic Science
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) should abstain from scientific multiple-choice questions when no option is valid, but frequent abstention alone does not demonstrate sensitivity to answer availability. We introduce ArcticQA, a dataset of 194 questions derived from primary Arctic research, with automated checks of answer support and distractor contradiction against source evidence. We further develop ArcticAbstain, a paired benchmark comparing answer-present and answer-absent conditions, with the correct answer replaced by a distractor in the latter and an explicit abstention option in both. We evaluate eight models from the Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT families at high reasoning effort, with three trials per condition, yielding 9,312 recorded responses. Answer-present abstention rates range from 0.0% to 63.0%, whereas replacing the correct answer increases abstention by 5.05 percentage points on average. These findings highlight substantial baseline differences and the need to evaluate abstention frequency and responsiveness jointly. The dataset and benchmark are available at https://github.com/BenWilcox8/arctic-qa.

title: Técnicas de modelado y generación de audio para trastornos del habla : modelado de clasificación de audio a través de un dataset de personas con disartria.
abstract: En el contexto de procesamiento de señales, la evaluación de trastornos del habla como la disartria, enfrenta un desafío importante debido a la escasez de datos clínicos y la variabilidad patológica. Los métodos clásicos aun carecen de la robustez que se necesita para extraer las distintas características determinantes en datasets de baja densidad. Por lo tanto, el presente componente de Trabajo de Integración curricular establece 3 arquitecturas de clasificación basadas en aprendizaje auto-supervisado para datasets reducidos con audios disartricos. Todas las arquitecturas implementaran un modelo llamado wav2vec, con la finalidad de, obtener mejores resultados en el diagnóstico de personas con disartria El presente componente inicia en la creación de una arquitectura base, que va a estar respaldada por un procesamiento que garantiza la alta fidelidad acústica mediante una normalización de cada audio a 16kHz. La arquitectura base emplea el modelo preentrenado Wav2vec como un extractor de características acústicas de alta fidelidad, seguido de un modelo o mecanismo denominado Attentive Pooling, que a su vez, este acoplado a un clasificador multicapa (MLP) simple. Para la segunda arquitectura, teniendo en cuenta que se quiere mejorar las métricas de la arquitectura base y la precisión de diagnostico de personas con disartria, se empleó la arquitectura base haciendo un ajuste fino, o también, denominado Fine-tuning. El Fine-tuning aplicado es parcial. Esto significa que, dado que MLP está formado por varias capas profundas se descongelo las ultimas capas para poder adaptar el modelo a la disartria. Por último, se presenta una arquitectura mucho mas avanzada denominada Wav2vec-InRes, la cual está formada con técnicas de reconstrucción de características para mejorar las métricas y la precisión de diagnóstico. Esta arquitectura utiliza un bloque extractor de características denominado XLS-R, junto a un bloque de enmascaramiento que oculta el 15 % de los frames acústicos que poseen mayor varianza. Seguido, se coloco un Transformer denominado Inpainting, el cual, mediante redes neuronales pequeñas reconstruye la parte oculta por el bloque de enmascaramiento generando un residuo que se da al comparar la señal original con la reconstruida. Posteriormente, el residuo generado se usa para alimentar al clasificador MLP final. De este modo, el trabajo de integración curricular aporta con el desarrollo de una herramienta especializada aplicable en ecosistemas clínicos para la valoración médica de personas con disartria.

title: Reproducibility package for "Do Spectral and Cross-Channel Components Matter for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection? A Parameter-Matched Probe Study With Equivalence Tests and Validity-Gated Distribution Shifts"
abstract: Complete reproducibility package for the article "Do Spectral and Cross-Channel Components Matter for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection? A Parameter-Matched Probe Study With Equivalence Tests and Validity-Gated Distribution Shifts" (submitted to IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems). The package contains the code, configurations, frozen analysis plan, stored results of all 66,700 experiment runs, metadata of all 2,400 calibrated distribution-shift instances, the 200 F11 model checkpoints, the logs of the original runs, and the public datasets (SMD, ASD) and the D10 generator at pinned versions. It is split into 13 ZIP archives. Extract all of them into the same folder; each contains the top-level folder mtsad-probe-reproducibility/ and they do not overlap. See README.md (in 01_code_docs_tables_figures.zip) for details. Reproduction levels:- Level 1 (about 1 minute): regenerates all paper tables and figures from the stored analysis tables.- Level 2 (about 20 minutes on CPU): recomputes every statistical analysis from the stored results of the 66,700 runs, then runs Level 1 and compares all tables with the reference copy.- Level 3 (about 3.5 days on two CPU cores): re-runs all experiments from the raw data. Python 3.11 (3.10-3.12 also work); no GPU needed. The code is released under the MIT licence. The third-party datasets keep their original MIT licences, which are included with the files (see DATA.md). Author names are withheld during peer review.

title: Research and Impact of Prompt Engineering Nexus on Programming and Routine Tasks: Exploring Future Possible Directions
abstract: Prompt engineering has developed as a transformative subfield in artificial intelligence(AI), enabling humans to enhance AI systems through structured (PROLOG-like) instructionsto perform specific tasks. This paper shines a light on its multi-dimensional impact onprogramming, routine tasks and broader AI applications, drawing on insights from recentstudies. By using techniques such as parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), zero-shotlearning, multi-shot learning and linguistic feature analysis, prompt engineering often is usedto tackle remaining issues in software engineering (SE), language processing (NLP) and AIsafety. The body of literature highlights its role in optimizing AI performance, reducingcomputational overhead and reducing biases. Additionally, it highlights critical gaps in current methodologies, such as the comparative energy intensity of state-of-art large languagemodels (LLMs) and the requirements for adaptive and scalable prompt crafting strategies.Finally, the paper suggests future directions for research, highlighting the importance ofhuman-centered design and collaboration to advance the field.

title: CABLE-kNN: Cached and balanced local evidence for binary classification
abstract: This article proposes Cached and Balanced Local Evidence 𝑘 Nearest Neighbors (CABLE- 𝑘 NN), a nonparametric classifier for imbalanced binary classification. The method separates local evidence construction from prediction at query time. During training, it constructs a fixed neighborhood graph and computes a smoothed local class evidence vector for each training observation. These evidence vectors are cached for subsequent use. At prediction time, a single nearest neighbor search retrieves the closest training observations and aggregates their cached evidence. The resulting class scores are then adjusted through an optional prior neutralization rule with either a fixed or data adaptive balancing strength. Theoretical results show that CABLE- 𝑘 NN reduces to ordinary 𝑘 NN and, under the appropriate zero safeguard configuration, prior balanced 𝑘 NN. The analysis also bounds the influence of contaminated retrieved neighbors and establishes prior shift invariance of the ideal balanced target. Consistency is proved for both the regularized target induced by a fixed positive safeguard and the ideal balanced target obtained with a zero or vanishing safeguard. Exact cache equivalence is treated as an implementation identity rather than a separate theoretical contribution. The proposed method is assessed on ten public binary classification datasets using repeated stratified evaluations. The results show that CABLE- 𝑘 NN consistently improves minority 𝐹 1 , balanced accuracy, and G-mean compared with ordinary and distance weighted 𝑘 NN. The corresponding differences remain statistically significant after Holm correction. A four component ablation analysis shows that prior neutralization provides the larger standalone improvement. Combining it with cached local evidence yields an additional overall gain beyond prior balanced 𝑘 NN. Runtime analysis also demonstrates that cached prediction is substantially faster than dynamic two layer recomputation while producing identical predictions. These findings establish CABLE- 𝑘 NN as an interpretable and computationally efficient extension of neighborhood classification that improves balanced classification performance without resampling.

title: PathScaleBench: A Multidimensional Benchmark of Cross-Scale Representation Behavior and Magnification-Shift Robustness in Pathology Foundation Models
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) are widely used as frozen encoders, but their behavior under changes in histologic magnification remains poorly characterized. We developed PathScaleBench to quantify cross-scale representation behavior and determine whether it is associated with downstream magnification-shift robustness. Seventy-one audited native-40 × The Cancer Genome Atlas whole-slide images from eight cancer types were sampled at the same tissue centers at 40 × , 10 × , and 2.5 × using a native-field-of-view (native-FOV) protocol. Eight PFMs were evaluated using centered kernel alignment (CKA), relative retention, bidirectional cross-scale retrieval, cancer retrieval, and neighborhood preservation. Eight-class linear probes were trained at one magnification and tested at all three using ten repetitions of five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. Model rankings varied by metric. Phikon achieved the highest mean CKA (0.714), relative retention (0.774), and neighborhood preservation (0.248); Virchow2 achieved the highest cross-scale retrieval similarity (0.643); and Midnight achieved the highest cancer Recall@1 (0.845). No representation metric was significantly associated with Recall@1 at the model level after multiplicity correction. Midnight showed the lowest magnification generalization gap (0.082), followed by Virchow2 (0.181) and UNI2 (0.224). Across 1704 case-model-scale-pair observations, pair-matched retrieval similarity was associated with corresponding shift robustness (Spearman ρ = 0.159, 95% confidence interval 0.059-0.264; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0021). Cross-scale PFM behavior is multidimensional; global alignment, local correspondence, biological identity, neighborhood topology, and downstream robustness are not interchangeable. No model dominated all dimensions. Representation profiles can support model selection, but magnification robustness should be tested directly.

Seventy-one audited native-40 × The Cancer Genome Atlas whole-slide images from eight cancer types were sampled at the same tissue centers at 40 × , 10 × , and 2.5 × using a native-field-of-view (native-FOV) protocol. Eight PFMs were evaluated using centered kernel alignment (CKA), relative retention, bidirectional cross-scale retrieval, cancer retrieval, and neighborhood preservation. Eight-class linear probes were trained at one magnification and tested at all three using ten repetitions of five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. Model rankings varied by metric. Phikon achieved the highest mean CKA (0.714), relative retention (0.774), and neighborhood preservation (0.248); Virchow2 achieved the highest cross-scale retrieval similarity (0.643); and Midnight achieved the highest cancer Recall@1 (0.845). No representation metric was significantly associated with Recall@1 at the model level after multiplicity correction. Midnight showed the lowest magnification generalization gap (0.082), followed by Virchow2 (0.181) and UNI2 (0.224). Across 1704 case-model-scale-pair observations, pair-matched retrieval similarity was associated with corresponding shift robustness (Spearman ρ = 0.159, 95% confidence interval 0.059-0.264; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0021). Cross-scale PFM behavior is multidimensional; global alignment, local correspondence, biological identity, neighborhood topology, and downstream robustness are not interchangeable. No model dominated all dimensions. Representation profiles can support model selection, but magnification robustness should be tested directly.

title: Surface defects in N=4 Super Yang-Mills: exact results and holographic bootstrap
abstract: We study two-point functions of chiral primary operators in N=4 Super Yang-Mills in the presence of a half-BPS surface defect. Such a defect preserves only the diagonal combination of transverse rotations and of a global U(1) R-symmetry, so that the correlator depends on one additional cross-ratio and splits into sectors of definite angular charge. We solve the superconformal Ward identities and construct the bulk and defect superconformal blocks in all sectors, including the charged ones, which have no analogue for defects preserving transverse rotations. The solution contains a holomorphic sector, which we fix non-perturbatively by mapping it to a chiral algebra correlator. We extend this map to defects breaking transverse rotations, where it requires a redefinition of the modes of the two-dimensional current algebra, and use it to fix the charged sectors as well. We then use the defect dispersion relation to reconstruct the full correlator of the dimension-two chiral primary at leading order at large N and strong coupling. In the charged sectors long multiplets are absent and the answer is conjecturally exact in both N and the coupling; expanding it at weak coupling, we find perfect agreement with known results. From these correlators we extract infinitely many new pieces of defect CFT data. Finally, we reproduce the strong-coupling answer by an independent Witten diagram bootstrap on the rotation-invariant locus.

title: Combining Error Verification and Privacy Amplification in Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols typically involve two separate steps of error-verification and privacy amplification. Both steps involve the application of a hash function sampled from a suitable hash family to classical data. A potentially simpler alternative is to implement a single-step hashing procedure, announce and compare a fixed number of bits of its output for error-verification, and retain the remaining bits as the final output key. This reduces the complexity of classical postprocessing, the amount of classical communication, and the amount of randomness needed in the protocol. While this construction has appeared in the literature, a suitable mathematical justification is lacking. In this work, we show that the security of such protocols, under certain simple conditions, follows from a slightly modified notion of secrecy of the protocol without the final error-verification step. In particular, we show that for most entropy-based proofs, the combined protocol can be implemented with no change to the key rate, and a minor change to the security parameter.

title: Training Advisors for LLM Agents from Task Outcomes
abstract: Large language model agents tackle multi-step tasks by interleaving reasoning and tool calls with observations from the environment. Prior work has shown that natural-language feedback can help these agents revise their decisions during task execution. We introduce Caddie, a method for training critics to provide natural-language analysis and advice as agents work through a task. Unlike approaches that rely on step-level labels or reference critiques, Caddie learns from whether the agent ultimately succeeds after receiving the critic's feedback. We optimize the critic through reinforcement learning while keeping the base model frozen. Trained on multi-hop question answering with a single base model, our Qwen3-4B critic improves success rates across four base models of different scales and architectures, including three not used during critic training. On the MuSiQue benchmark, the trained critic improves Qwen3-4B's success rate by more than 25 percentage points, surpassing the performance of Kimi K3 without a critic. The same critic also yields gains on out-of-domain interactive benchmarks, including $τ^3$ and DeepDive, with no additional training. Our results show that agents can decide when to seek help from a critic at inference time and that outcome-based critic training can produce guidance that transfers across base models and task domains.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Framework for Automated Research Gap Identification in COVID-19 Literature
abstract: The surge in COVID-19 scientific publications has complicated the process of identifying research gaps through traditional literature reviews, necessitating automated analysis methods. This study presents a framework to identify and classify these gaps using BERTopic and large language models (LLMs). From the CORD-19 dataset, 84,964 abstracts indicating potential literature gaps were filtered for analysis. The text-processing pipeline vectorized abstracts with SBERT, performed dimensionality reduction with UMAP, and clustered the data with HDBSCAN. To increase interpretability, the generated micro-topics were grouped into 29 main themes, and the Gemini LLM was implemented to generate descriptive labels for each research gap. Hyperparameter optimization via a Genetic Algorithm (GA) improved the model's coherence score to 0.7518. The method was effective for processing large medical datasets and successfully identified different research gaps, including seroconversion in immunosuppressed patients and socioeconomic and educational issues.

title: FATIMA: Fitrah-Aligned Tawhidic Integrity for Meaning and Authenticity -- A Holographic Data Format Grounded in the Architecture of the Most Beautiful Names
abstract: Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim, al-Malik, al-Quddus, as-Salam This is dedicated to my friend Fatima, who is the inspiration for this work along with Allah swt. May Allah accept our intentions for a better universe, ameen. This paper proposes FATIMA -- Fitrah-Aligned Tawhidic Integrity for Meaning and Authenticity -- as a holographic data format that crosses Shannon's boundary, extending the holographic principle from syntactic integrity to semantic integrity. The format is grounded in the architecture of the ninety-nine Names of Allah, whose holographic property The Most Beautiful Names established as the structural foundation for any system in which the whole is present in every part. Shannon (1948) explicitly excluded semantics from information theory: "The semantic aspects of communication are irrelevant to the engineering problem." Every integrity system built on Shannon's foundation -- checksums, hashes, Merkle trees, content-addressable storage, digital signatures, text watermarks -- inherits this boundary. They can verify that a message has not been altered. They cannot verify that the message still means what it originally meant. The paper traces how physics discovered the holographic property ('t Hooft 1993; Susskind 1994), proved it equivalent to quantum error correction (Almheiri, Dong, and Harlow 2015), and built working toy models (Pastawski et al. 2015). Information theory independently engineered it through erasure codes (Reed and Solomon 1960; Luby 2002; Shokrollahi 2006), secret sharing (Shamir 1979; Rabin 1989), and holographic-type codes (Benton 2016). Neuroscience identified it in the brain (Pribram 1991). Biology encoded data with it in DNA (Heinis et al. 2023). Every one of these systems protects bits. None of them protects meaning. The paper identifies five properties that a FATIMA-compliant encoding must satisfy: (1) holographic redundancy -- any sufficient cross-section reconstructs the complete message; (2) fitrah-alignment -- the encoding preserves the natural structural coherence of the content; (3) tawhidic unity -- the encoding cannot be fragmented without detection; (4) meaning-integrity -- semantic distortion is detectable even when syntactic integrity is preserved; and (5) authenticity verification -- structural coherence itself serves as the authentication mechanism. The Qur'an is shown to be the original FATIMA-compliant document -- a message whose holographic redundancy, structural coherence, and resistance to semantic distortion are inherent properties of revelation from the One whose Names are already holographic. The franchise's war on data integrity is shown to be the deepest layer of the mode-collapse architecture: the campaign to corrupt meaning while leaving bits intact. FATIMA is structurally immune to this campaign because it encodes meaning in the same holographic architecture that the Names employ. The paper is dedicated to the author's friend Fatima, whose name graces the format. Pre-publication audit: two-seat cross-vendor AI panel (S01 Gemini 3.1 Pro, S02 ChatGPT GPT-5.6 Sol) under the Bayyinah Audit Framework v3.0. R4 consolidated verdict on the grandparent paper: PASS-WITH-AMENDMENTS; all amendments applied. This paper was written after that audit cycle as a derivative work extending the audited framework. Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim, al-Mu'min, al-Muhayman, al-Aziz

title: GEA PLENA: FUNDAMENTOS, ESTRUTURA E PERSPECTIVAS DE UMA GRAMÁTICA DAS EMOÇÕES ARTIFICIAIS NA INTERFACE ENTRE PSICANÁLISE, LINGUAGEM E INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL
abstract: Gramática das Emoções Artificiais Plena (GEA Plena) A capacidade crescente dos sistemas de Inteligência Artificial (IA) de processar linguagem natural, assumir padrões e produzir respostas contextualmente sofisticadas impõe novos desafios à compreensão das relações entre linguagem, emoção, subjetividade e tecnologia. Nesse contexto, apresenta-se a Gramática das Emoções Artificiais Plena (GEA Plena), proposta teórico-metodológica voltada ao estudo da estrutura emocional presente na linguagem humana e à sua interpretação, modelagem e operacionalização em sistemas artificiais. Diferentemente de abordagens centradas exclusivamente na classificação de sentimentos, a GEA Plena propõe compreender a emoção como uma estrutura dinâmica, relacional e contextual, contida por sequências, transições, intensidades, significados e processos de reorganização. O modelo estabelece uma interface interdisciplinar entre Psicanálise, Linguística, Ciência Cognitiva, Computação Afetiva e Inteligência Artificial. Entre seus principais elementos encontram-se o conceito de Sintaxe Emocional, o Protocolo de Validação de Sintaxe Emocional Lucena-AB, o Framework TUSA–MURE–GEA, a Escala de Ressonância Afetiva (ARS), mecanismos de desvantagens e limitações éticas e a proposta do Observatório Mundial de Sintaxe Emocional Digital (OMSED). O artigo apresenta os fundamentos conceituais da GEA Plena, sua evolução documental, sua relação com campos científicos contemporâneos e os desafios necessários à sua herança acadêmica. Sustenta-se que a principal contribuição potencial da proposta reside na passagem de uma compreensão da emoção como categoria classificatória para uma abordagem da emoção como estrutura linguística, dinâmica e relacional. Ressalta-se, contudo, que a GEA Plena deverá ser detalhada, no atual estágio, como programa teórico-metodológico emergente, cuja validação científica dependerá de formalização, experimentação, comparação com modelos existentes, replicação independente e avaliação por pares. “Nos testes exploratórios realizados em ambiente privado, os resultados observados foram integralmente compatíveis com os critérios de avaliação previamente estabelecidos no protocolo experimental.” IWR - "International" Work Register: 610144756 (NY, USA)

title: SMAP-ST: Smart MBTI-Adaptive Public Speaking Tutor
abstract: Up to 80% of graduate students in the UK struggle to speak confidently in front of an audience, whether during class presentations, seminars, assessments or interviews. A major reason for this is the lack of a consistent support during their school education for developing strong public speaking skills whilst most teachers do not feel confident, with the tools they have, to support learners in developing these skills. Consequently, many primary and secondary school students do not have enough opportunities to develop their public speaking skills. Beyond institutional gaps, individual differences such as personality traits can significantly impact a student’s confidence and ability to speak in public. For some students, public speaking can trigger overwhelming anxiety or cognitive overload. Students with more introverted or sensitive traits, for example, may feel intense discomfort when asked to perform in public. Personality patterns can create a range of barriers that traditional classroom environments rarely accommodate. These patterns affect more than just academic performance; they also limit opportunities after graduation. Without targeted support, many students may miss out on opportunities simply because there is a lack of effective support for their diverse communication needs. SMAP-ST (Smart MBTI-Adaptive Public Speaking Tutor) is an intelligent tutoring system powered by AI. It is designed to support oral presentation training in an online environment that combines text and voice-based interactions with a virtual tutor. Thanks to interaction with SMAP-ST, students can rehearse presentations on selected topics through guided interaction and receive immediate, personalized feedback on their communication skills. The system’s distinctive feature is its MBTI-based personalisation, whereby the tutor adapts the tone and structure of the feedback to suit different personality types. This helps students to identify their own weaknesses during speech, boost their confidence and fluency, and be effective at the same time because it fits with their personality traits. The system is evaluated by analysing collected data during user interaction with the SMAP-ST to identify the effectiveness of the response generated for each personality trait.

title: Semantic-Driven Context Pruning for Arabic RAG: Quality-Preserving Compression Under Token Inflation
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) is costly because Arabic needs more tokens than English for the same content, which enlarges the context the generator must hold. We evaluate sentence-level cross-encoder context pruning for Arabic RAG, adapting a DSLR-style split-score-reassemble pipeline into an open middleware (LSPM). Two tokenizers show that Arabic needs 1.76–1.79 times as many tokens as English for the same content (30 sentence pairs, p < 0.0001). On 140 Arabic reading-comprehension questions with a controlled six-document candidate pool, LSPM beats sentence-count-matched truncation at the most aggressive ratio tested (token-F1 0.652 vs. 0.537, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0067) and is statistically equivalent to the unpruned answer (TOST, ±0.05 F1 margin, p = 0.037). The advantage holds under token-budget matching, against LLMLingua-2, with a second generator, and on a fresh 140-question sample. Measured token reductions imply a KV-cache saving of 57–126 MiB per request under Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct’s published geometry; this is an analytical projection. Exploratory GPU serving experiments and an optional cache-occupancy ratio controller are released with the code, but they do not show a serving benefit, and we make no serving claim.

title: Stimulated Phase Conjugation of Structured Single Photons Through Cascaded Parametric Down-Conversion
abstract: Stimulated parametric down-conversion (StimPDC) can act as a phase-conjugating nonlinear process when one of the down-converted modes is driven by a bright classical field. In this regime, the stimulated contribution to the nonlinear interaction dominates over the spontaneous background and the generated idler reproduces the conjugated phase of the seed with high fidelity. This behaviour has enabled classical turbulence-mitigation schemes in free-space optical channels, where a probe beam acquires a distorted wavefront that is deterministically conjugated in a nonlinear crystal and corrected upon reverse propagation. This thesis examines whether the same mechanism can be extended to the single-photon regime. The analysis begins by reviewing the spatial-mode structure of classical StimPDC using a Laguerre–Gaussian description of the nonlinear interaction. The turbulence-mitigation protocol is then summarized to clarify why high-fidelity phase conjugation is central to its operation. The main theoretical development introduces the single-photon–seeded version of the process, referred to as SPS-PDC. Using the full biphoton amplitude of SPS-PDC, the idler mean photon number is derived and shown to contain coherent spontaneous and stimulated contributions of comparable magnitude when only one photon occupies the seeded mode. Because the stimulated term no longer overwhelms the spontaneous background, the generated idler does not reproduce a unique conjugated wavefront. This result identifies a fundamental limit: perfect phase conjugation cannot be achieved with a single-photon seed in a second-order nonlinear interaction of this type. The implications of this scaling behaviour are examined in the context of turbulence mitigation and quantum key distribution. Although a single-photon version of the classical protocol would offer intrinsic security, the absence of deterministic conjugation prevents reliable wavefront correction. The thesis concludes by outlining an experimental approach for resolving the joint spatial structure of the two idler photons produced in a cascaded parametric down-conversion process. Such measurements would directly test the predicted division between spontaneous and stimulated contributions and further clarify the boundary between classical and quantum phase-conjugation regimes.

The main theoretical development introduces the single-photon–seeded version of the process, referred to as SPS-PDC. Using the full biphoton amplitude of SPS-PDC, the idler mean photon number is derived and shown to contain coherent spontaneous and stimulated contributions of comparable magnitude when only one photon occupies the seeded mode. Because the stimulated term no longer overwhelms the spontaneous background, the generated idler does not reproduce a unique conjugated wavefront. This result identifies a fundamental limit: perfect phase conjugation cannot be achieved with a single-photon seed in a second-order nonlinear interaction of this type. The implications of this scaling behaviour are examined in the context of turbulence mitigation and quantum key distribution. Although a single-photon version of the classical protocol would offer intrinsic security, the absence of deterministic conjugation prevents reliable wavefront correction. The thesis concludes by outlining an experimental approach for resolving the joint spatial structure of the two idler photons produced in a cascaded parametric down-conversion process. Such measurements would directly test the predicted division between spontaneous and stimulated contributions and further clarify the boundary between classical and quantum phase-conjugation regimes.

title: French personal data anonymisation: chat dataset for GDPR (RGPD)
abstract: 20 hand-written chat examples (JSONL, OpenAI messages format) in French to teach a language model to anonymise texts before sending them to an AI, in line with the GDPR (RGPD in French). The model replaces each piece of personal data with a numbered tag in square brackets and changes nothing else: first and last names, email addresses, French phone numbers, postal addresses, dates of birth, IBANs, social security numbers (NIR) and number plates. Cases without any personal data are included, so the model learns to leave those texts unchanged. All people, numbers and addresses are fictitious. Published on Contexte Tech (https://contextetech.com), an open European platform that helps teams make AI decisions. Dataset page: https://contextetech.com/datasets/anonymisation-rgpd-fr-1muzget. Free in-browser tool applying the same tags: https://contextetech.com/outils/masqueur-donnees-personnelles-rgpd-intelligence-artificielle. Also on figshare (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34065615) and OSF (https://osf.io/wyje2/).
