title: A privacy preserving federated deep learning system for early financial fraud detection and prevention
abstract: Traditional rule-based and classical machine learning approaches have been rendered insufficient in terms of adaptability, scalability, and detection accuracy due to the significant challenge posed by the rapid growth of digital financial transactions and the increasing sophistication of fraudulent activities. Additionally, centralized data aggregation introduces critical privacy, security, and regulatory concerns, which restrict real-world deployment and cross-institutional collaborations. This study proposes FL-E $$F^2$$ DP, a privacy-preserving and robust framework that integrates deep learning and federated learning for the early detection and prevention of financial fraud, as a solution to these challenges. The proposed architecture utilizes convolutional neural networks to autonomously acquire hierarchical feature representations from high-dimensional transactional data, thereby facilitating the precise identification of intricate and evolving fraud patterns. Federated learning enables the collaborative training of models across distributed financial institutions without the exchange of raw transaction data, thereby guaranteeing data confidentiality, regulatory compliance, and improves system robustness. In addition, the framework integrates automated mitigation unified risk fusion, guideline-based control verification, and recommendation reporting to offer proactive fraud prevention and comprehensive risk assessment. The proposed approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, as evidenced by extensive experiments conducted on a widely used CCFD and PSFD datasets. This approach achieves superior accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The effectiveness, scalability, and reliability of the proposed framework for real-world financial fraud detection in secure and distributed environments are validated by these results.

title: Primordial black holes as a natural consequence of scale-invariance
abstract: We show that a scale-invariant U(1) gauge theory can naturally realize large curvature perturbations around the end of thermal inflation, seeding the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). The allowed nonminimal gravitational interaction ξ of the Higgs field induces a Hubble-scale negative mass-squared term for positive ξsim O(1), and triggers a second order phase transition that ends thermal inflation while keeping the extra e-folds small. This sharp contrast to the minimally coupled case allows the gauge coupling to be much smaller than unity. It turns out that field fluctuations are dominated by thermal fluctuations around the onset of the phase transition, and sufficiently amplified to produce an appreciable amount of PBHs with a wide range of possible masses. The associated scalar-induced gravitational waves (GWs) are accompanied by cosmic-string induced GWs coming from the breaking of the U(1) symmetry. As a result, the generated PBH population can have a correlated GW signature relevant to pulsar timing arrays, space-based interferometers, or ground-based detectors.

title: Derivative Gaussian Processes on a Two-Direction Budget
abstract: Gradient observations promise more accurate Gaussian process (GP) surrogates, but the cost of incorporating them has long stood in the way of realizing that promise. We propose a derivative GP with a budget of just two directions per observed gradient. One direction focuses on each gradient's direct contribution to target prediction, while the other aggregates its indirect contributions through correlations with the conditioning function values. Within a Vecchia approximation, where each prediction conditions on $m$ nearby inputs in $d$ dimensions, this construction represents their $md$ gradient coordinates using at most $2m$ directional derivatives, giving $\mathcal{O}(m^3)$ dense factorization cost per prediction target. For general conditioning sets, we bound the posterior approximation error relative to using full gradients and characterize when the error is small or the approximation is exact. In simulations, our method matches the accuracy of a leading exact gradient-reduction method at equal conditioning set size. Because its cost grows much more slowly with that size, it can use conditioning sets well beyond the memory limit of the exact method, reaching lower prediction error with a small fraction of the time and memory. Notably, our method can exploit gradient observations while requiring less computation time or memory than function-only GP baselines.

title: Encoding–Noise Interaction in Hybrid Quantum Classifiers: A Registered Simulation Study with Convergence Audit
abstract: Comparisons of quantum data-encoding strategies are rarely accompanied by a registered estimand, an explicit treatment of where simulated noise is applied, or a classical reference point. This study reports a registered simulation study of the interaction between data encoding (angle versus ZZ feature map) and circuit noise (noiseless versus single-Pauli errors with probability p = 0.02 after every CNOT, plus readout flips) for an 8-qubit variational quantum classifier trained with SPSA. Three binary datasets, ten confirmatory seeds (240 runs) and circuit size as a secondary factor were used. Hyperparameters were tuned symmetrically on separate seeds and frozen before the confirmatory runs. The registered primary estimand, the Encoding x Noise interaction on validation balanced accuracy, was -0.154 (95% seed-cluster bootstrap CI [-0.181, -0.124]), which supports the registered directional hypothesis. ZZ-encoded models trained under noise met the pre-declared convergence criterion in 1 of 60 runs, against 48 of 60 for angle encoding, so training failure and signal degradation are not separated by the registered design. An exploratory follow-up, in which ZZ models were trained without noise and evaluated under noise, showed accuracy falling to 0.55-0.63 at p = 0.02, which points to the number of noisy two-qubit gates (56 additional CNOTs) as the main driver. The registered transfer hypothesis was not supported: robust selection did not differ from naive selection (+0.003, CI [-0.012, +0.016]). A class-balanced logistic regression exceeded every quantum configuration on validation accuracy. No quantum advantage is claimed.

title: Artifact for Trees, Walks, and Words: A Logic for File System Interactions
abstract: Programs often interface with file systems for a variety of tasks, from retrieving and storing computation data to configuring the operating system. These interactions are mediated by paths, and the complex interplay between programs, paths, and hierarchical file system state can lead to unexpected behaviors ranging from silent failures to irreversible data loss and security vulnerabilities. Yet, this domain remains underserved by formal reasoning. This paper addresses that gap by developing foundations for automated formal analysis of file-system-interacting programs. Grounding our study in a survey of APIs across several widely used standard libraries, we distill core file system behaviors into a representative object language, WhileFS . We then develop a theory of tree-walking word equations (TWE) and show that it is adequate to reason about file system interactions via sound and complete symbolic semantics for WhileFS . We demonstrate that the satisfiability question for TWE is as hard as the longstanding open problem of word equations with length constraints. Nonetheless, we also show that two useful fragments remain decidable in PSPACE by reduction to standard word equation theories. Together, these results demonstrate that TWE and WhileFS constitute a rich foundation for formal reasoning about programs that interact with file systems.

title: Adaptive Information-Theoretic Boundary Regularization for Dynamic Decision Thresholding in Severely Imbalanced Classification
abstract: Adaptive Information-Theoretic Boundary Regularization for Dynamic Decision Thresholding in Severely Imbalanced Classification Michael Allan A. Bahtaji, Ph.D. Department of Physics, College of Science Technological University of the Philippines Ayala Boulevard, Ermita, Manila, Philippines, 1000 Email: michaelallan_bahtaji@tup.edu.ph | michaelallanbahtaji336@gmail.com Abstract In probabilistic binary classification under severe class imbalance (), the default decision threshold fails to maximize Macro -score and Precision-Recall operating metrics due to posterior probability compression toward zero. In this paper, we propose an information-theoretic post-processing framework that dynamically calibrates decision cutoffs without retraining the underlying classifier. We introduce the Adaptive Boundary Operator , which maps empirical class imbalance ratios (calibrated on training/validation partitions) and prediction entropy directly into a cost-weighted threshold boundary. We mathematically prove that for classifiers exhibiting negative skew under class imbalance, the -optimal decision cutoff strictly satisfies , and we define as a Bayesian cost-weighted surrogate estimator. Furthermore, by applying a continuous probability score re-mapping , our framework expands the continuous precision-recall envelope. Extensive empirical benchmarks across three public imbalanced datasets—Credit Card Fraud Detection (), Medical Disease Risk (), and Long-Tail CIFAR-10 ()—demonstrate that our adaptive thresholding method consistently outperforms default cutoffs, Youden’s -statistic, and Precision-Recall break-even baselines, achieving a Macro -score of , Balanced Accuracy of , and recalibrated PR-AUC of on severe fraud detection tasks. Keywords: Class Imbalance, Dynamic Decision Thresholding, Precision-Recall Optimization, -Score Maximization, Information Theory, Probability Score Recalibration.

title: Gayrimenkul CRM'lerinde Yapay Zekâ Destekli Lead Nitelendirmesi için Yönetişim Kontrol Listesi ve Kademeli Devreye Alma Protokolü: Niyet Çıkarımı, Önceliklendirme, Mesaj Taslağı ve Kayıp Riski Uyarılarında İnsan Denetimi, Kayıt Tutma ve Hata Yönetimi
abstract: Gayrimenkul satış ekipleri, reklam formlarından, ilan portallarından ve WhatsApp'tan gelen serbest metinli talepleri büyük dil modelleri (LLM) ile işleyerek CRM alanlarını doldurmaya, adayları önceliklendirmeye, temsilciye görüşme notu ve mesaj taslağı hazırlamaya ve olumsuz duygu içeren mesajlarda yöneticiyi uyarmaya başlamıştır. korayyalcin.org üzerindeki uygulama yazıları bu senaryoların nasıl kurulacağını anlatmakta, ancak bu kararların kim tarafından, hangi sınırlar içinde, hangi kayıtlarla ve hata durumunda nasıl yönetileceğini tek bir çerçevede ele almamaktadır. Bu çerçeve notu söz konusu boşluğa yönelik iki araç önerir. Birincisi, sekiz alanda toplanmış ve her maddesi bir kontrol sorusu ile beklenen kanıttan oluşan bir yönetişim kontrol listesidir (YZ-LYK). İkincisi, yapay zekâ çıktısının iş akışındaki etkisini dört özerklik düzeyinde sınıflandıran ve gölge moddan sınırlı otomasyona kademeli geçişi tarif eden bir devreye alma protokolüdür. Belge, müşteriye giden içeriklerin ve bir adayı takipten çıkaran kararların insan onayı olmadan verilmemesi, model çağrısının ilk temas süresini hiçbir koşulda geciktirmemesi ve her yapay zekâ kararının model ile istem sürümüyle birlikte kayda geçirilmesi ilkelerini temel alır. Çalışma belge temelli kavramsal bir tasarımdır; ampirik veri, örneklem veya performans iddiası içermez ve hukuki görüş niteliği taşımaz. Kontrol listesinin geçerliliği ve kullanılabilirliği gelecekteki saha uygulamalarıyla sınanmalıdır.

title: The Model-Infrastructure Co-Evolution in Conversational NLU: From ELIZA to Large Language Models
abstract: Conversational Natural Language Understanding (NLU) has passed through five distinguishable technological eras: rule-based symbolic parsing, statistical and probabilistic modelling, neural sequence learning, Transformer-based pretraining, and the current large language model regime. Existing accounts of this history tend to foreground modelling advances and treat infrastructure as a supporting detail. This article argues instead that the two tracks are causally entangled: each scientific advance in conversational NLU became production-viable only once a matching infrastructure capability, spanning hardware, data pipelines, training paradigms, and serving architecture, made it deployable at scale, and each infrastructure capability in turn exposed the next scientific bottleneck. The analysis traces a specific bottleneck sequence, from combinatorial rule brittleness through representational discreteness, vanishing gradients, and sequential processing limits, to labelled-data scarcity, showing how each resolution reshaped the engineering problems that remained. A closing synthesis argues that large language models have not simplified conversational architecture; they have relocated its complexity from authoring rules and training classifiers toward orchestration, retrieval grounding, and failure isolation across distributed inference systems. The account draws on systems-architecture reasoning applied to the published research and technical-report record, rather than on a new empirical benchmark.

title: Feature selection in cluster analysis for functional data with application to the labour market in Poland
abstract: The aim of this article is to apply methods of cluster analysis to functional data in order to determine if there are homogeneous groups among the provinces of Poland in terms of 20 features related to the labour market. In some existing studies all available features are used for cluster analysis, even though some of them may be insignificant for the task. Irrelevant features have a negative impact on the complexity and performance of clustering algorithms. In this study, before clusters of provinces were identified, features significantly differentiating provinces were selected. Our new feature selection criterion involves the use of coefficients of functional distance correlation and functional Hilbert-Schmidt correlation between the features characterizing provinces and their labels. The resulting clusters were nearly identical regardless of whether all 20 features were used or just the 9 significant ones, which indicates that irrelevant features do not contribute much to cluster identification. The methodology proposed in this article is flexible and can be successfully used in other research areas including, inter alia, poverty, socio-economic development or disability.

title: BEANS-Next and ROOTS: Broadening Audio-Language Capabilities for Bioacoustics
abstract: Bioacoustics and ethology encompass a wide range of audio understanding tasks, many of which stand to benefit from recent advances in large audio-language models. However, progress in the field has so far been assessed on a narrow set of tasks, primarily centered on label-centric biological category recognition, such as species and call-type classification. In this work, we introduce BEANS-Next, a benchmark grounded in a taxonomy of bioacoustics tasks spanning acoustic perception, biological category recognition, scene understanding, and in-context learning. Using BEANS-Next, we show that existing models exhibit limited performance beyond the task families emphasized by existing evaluations, constraining their usefulness for broader bioacoustic applications. To support progress on this broader task space, we also introduce ROOTS, a large-scale training resource built from expanded curated real-world data and previously underused behavioral and acoustic metadata, supplemented by audio-derived information and scalable synthetic generation where labeling is insufficient. We demonstrate that training on this dataset yields substantial progress across all task groups of BEANS-Next, moving audio-language models closer to their potential as general-purpose assistants for bioacoustics and ethology. To accelerate progress in the field, we open-source our benchmark, dataset, and data pipelines.

In this work, we introduce BEANS-Next, a benchmark grounded in a taxonomy of bioacoustics tasks spanning acoustic perception, biological category recognition, scene understanding, and in-context learning. Using BEANS-Next, we show that existing models exhibit limited performance beyond the task families emphasized by existing evaluations, constraining their usefulness for broader bioacoustic applications. To support progress on this broader task space, we also introduce ROOTS, a large-scale training resource built from expanded curated real-world data and previously underused behavioral and acoustic metadata, supplemented by audio-derived information and scalable synthetic generation where labeling is insufficient. We demonstrate that training on this dataset yields substantial progress across all task groups of BEANS-Next, moving audio-language models closer to their potential as general-purpose assistants for bioacoustics and ethology. To accelerate progress in the field, we open-source our benchmark, dataset, and data pipelines.

title: Shared Gaussianization: What Gaussian Regularizers Certify About Contrastive Learning, and What They Miss
abstract: What can a distribution-matching regularizer such as SIGReg in LeJEPA certify about contrastive learning? We study shared Gaussianization (SG), a characteristic-function Gaussianity test on the average of two normalized views, scaled by an independent $χ_d$ radius. Because disagreeing views shorten the average, one test detects both misalignment and non-uniformity. SG vanishes exactly at the aligned, uniform minimizers of population InfoNCE, and under equal marginals it bounds the InfoNCE excess by $4\cdot 3^{3/4}β$ times the square root of the SG loss, plus a term linear in the loss. The square-root rate and this dimension-free constant are sharp, and no squared mean-embedding distance on view pairs achieves a faster rate. With an explicit alignment term, a rotation-invariant uniformity test gives a linear bound if and only if its spectrum dominates that of InfoNCE's kernel $e^{βu^\top v}$; SG's own test does, Gaussian kernels $e^{-γ\|u-v\|^2}$ qualify exactly when $γ\ge β/2$, and moment matching never does. Away from the optimum, the objectives differ. Along an isotropic nuisance channel, pure SG lowers its loss by adding per-view nuisance whenever the shared code is non-uniform. An alignment weight above the channel's gain makes the nuisance-free solution a strict local minimizer; for LeJEPA, the same rule gives a critical SIGReg weight that decreases with the batch size. At finite batch size, an off-diagonal U-statistic removes a plug-in bias toward misalignment. In controlled latent-variable models, pure SG retains per-view style, an alignment weight above the measured gain removes it, and for LeJEPA at three batch sizes the measured gain separates the encoders that retain style from those that do not. InfoNCE training also reaches a lower SG$_{0.2}$ loss than SG$_{0.2}$ training from scratch, which points to an optimization gap.

title: Gauss-Newton Accuracy and Indefinite Hessians: Uniform Coexistence in Low-Cost Sets
abstract: We study the accuracy of Gauss-Newton curvature in ridge-regularized nonlinear least squares. Under local regularity and persistence of level-set curvature magnitude along an exact-fit section, we prove uniform coexistence of two curvature regimes. Global minimizers exist, and every global minimizer has relative Hessian error below (1+sqrt2)/8, while the same low-cost set contains a point with an indefinite Hessian and relative error at least 15/8. One positive ridge cap works for all independent center and label perturbations in fixed neighborhoods and every positive ridge weight up to the cap. These neighborhoods do not shrink as the ridge weight tends to zero. A pointwise certificate based on the current prediction level set controls the normal, mixed, and tangent parts of the Hessian correction. We prove a sharp relative-error bound over the stated pointwise class when the prediction map and ridge vary. Analytic examples describe the roles of output alignment, curvature orientation, and persistence. A separate structural result gives full Jacobian row rank throughout low-cost sets and exact interpolation near a rank-deficient reference.

title: КОРПУС ЯК ДЗЕРКАЛО КОЛЕКТИВНОГО КОГНІТИВНОГО ДОСВІДУ В КОНТЕКСТІ РОЗВИТКУ МОВНИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ (2020–2025)
abstract: In the context of developing large language models (LLMs) between 2020 and 2025, the article provides a thorough examination of the evolution of corpus linguistics in Ukraine through the lens of the linguo-cognitive dimension. The research investigates the development of of natural language processing tools, linguistic annotation techniques, and Ukrainian corpus resources that serve as the foundation for training contemporary language models. The emergence of domestic artificial intelligence architectures, particularly MamayLM and Lapa LLM, and the dynamic transformation of corpus data are highlighted as ways that they reflect the national communicative space and contribute to the development of a digital linguistic worldview of Ukrainian society. The idea that the linguistic corpus is an objective “mirror” of collective cognitive experience that accumulates mental structures is grounded by the author. The article identifies key linguistic challenges of the Ukrainian language for natural language processing systems, including high inflectional complexity, morphological variability, and flexible syntax. These features show up as manifestations of particular cognitive mechanisms of speech organization rather than just as technical challenges for NLP models. In order to help language models better understand the context and pragmatics of Ukrainian speech, the study examines contemporary corpus labelling techniques, such as multi-level annotation of grammatical, semantic, and emotional text parameters. It is argued that the creation of national corpora and large language models is an essential factor in ensuring the cognitive security and digital sovereignty of Ukraine, as it facilitates the representation of unique cultural and linguistic experiences in the global information space and forms the foundation for the further development of Ukrainian artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection
abstract: Normative State Locking and Bounded Activation Dynamics: An Information-Theoretic Boundary Framework for Self-Defending AI and Information Theft Protection Michael Allan A. Bahtaji, Ph.D. Department of Physics, College of Science Technological University of the Philippines Ayala Boulevard, Ermita, Manila, Philippines, 1000 Email: michaelallan_bahtaji@tup.edu.ph | michaelallanbahtaji336@gmail.com Abstract Artificial intelligence models and distributed machine learning infrastructures face persistent security risks, including gradient instability, adversarial prompt injections, model inversion, and automated data exfiltration. In this paper, we present a mathematically rigorous, self-contained information-theoretic boundary framework that addresses deep learning gradient stability and active model theft defense within a unified architecture. First, we introduce the -Bounded Activation Function (), parameterized as , where functions as a dynamic finite boundary cutoff scale initialized at and optimized dynamically via backpropagation. We formally prove that possesses a Lipschitz continuous derivative bounded within , eliminating gradient vanishing and exploding phenomena. Second, to protect model weights, proprietary training data, and user privacy from invasive queries, we formulate the Intent Discrimination Index () as a trace-parity check over measurement density operators constructed explicitly via normalized rank-one projection states . When invasive probing or unauthorized extraction is detected (), calibrated on an independent validation partition (), the architecture activates a Normative State Locking Protocol, executing a decision-theoretic state projection to the decoupled ground vacuum state . We provide complete analytical proofs, algorithmic pseudocode, PyTorch implementations, and empirical benchmark evaluations demonstrating training convergence stability and near-perfect detection of adversarial exfiltration queries. Keywords: Information Theft Protection, Cybersecurity, Self-Defending AI, Bounded Activation Function (), Normative State Locking, Quantum Bayesianism (QBism), Model Inversion Defense, Gradient Stability.

title: Introduction to entanglement-assisted quantum error correction from pre-quantum mathematical literature
abstract: The presentation file consists of two parts. In Part 1: Overlooked incompatibility between finite fields and quantum error correction with its remedies, we give a simple counterexample to the popular definition of quantum stabilizer codes invoving finite fields, and review two mathematically correct ways to define them. In Part 2: Introduction to entanglement-assisted quantum error correction from pre-quantum mathematical literature, based on Part 1 we introduce entanglement-assisted quantum error correction by using as much finite fields and as little complex vectors/matrices as possible, which is hopefully more friendly to classical coding theorests. We also clarify the connection to pre-quantum mathematical literature. These slides will be used in a workshop held on November 2026 at Castelló University Institute of Mathematics and Applications (IMAC), Universitat Jaume I, Spain. Version 1 has redundant assumptions in the Witt extension theorem, which are removed in version 2. The other file consists of mathematical proofs omitted from the presentation. It is generated by AI.

title: RG-SCSO: source code, seeds, and raw per-run results for relevance-guided parsimonious feature selection
abstract: This dataset provides the complete, reproducible research artifacts for the study "Relevance-Guided Binarization for Parsimonious Feature Selection with Sand Cat Swarm Optimization" (RG-SCSO). RG-SCSO replaces the fixed, feature-agnostic transfer function used by swarm-based binary feature selectors with a per-feature, relevance-modulated binarization that injects a mutual-information prior directly at the bit-decision step.

title: Correlation-aware measurement fusion for reliable cooperative 3D target tracking in connected autonomous vehicles
abstract: Abstract Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) can improve target tracking by sharing distributed measurements of surrounding traffic participants. However, cooperative measurement fusion is reliable only when both measurement uncertainty and inter-vehicle dependence are properly modelled. Sequential Kalman filtering provides a communication-efficient late-fusion solution for cooperative target tracking, but its standard formulation relies on statistically independent and temporally aligned measurements. In practical connected-vehicle systems, this assumption can be violated by shared detection algorithms, common environmental conditions, and communication delay. As a result, correlated or temporally misaligned measurements may be repeatedly counted, leading to underestimated covariance and overconfident target-state estimates. This paper proposes ReCoTrack, a correlation-aware measurement fusion framework for reliable cooperative 3D target tracking. ReCoTrack preserves the association advantages of sequential Kalman filtering while selectively applying covariance intersection (CI) to targets jointly observed by multiple vehicles. This design enables conservative state fusion under unknown inter-vehicle measurement correlations. To improve uncertainty propagation, a trajectory-based process-noise estimator is further introduced to learn motion-dependent covariance from historical target states. An innovation-consistency objective is also designed to jointly calibrate observation and process noise covariances. Experiments on the V2V4Real dataset show that the proposed method improves Average Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (AMOTA) by 2.8%, increases mostly tracked trajectories by 4.5%, and reduces mostly lost trajectories by 10.9% under the same late-fusion communication setting, while evaluation on OPV2V under a unified tracking protocol shows that ReCoTrack achieves the highest AMOTA among the compared methods and outperforms DMSTrack by 1.05 percentage points. The framework requires only 0.0073 MB per CAV per frame. Additional tests under controlled cross-CAV dependence and stochastic communication degradation demonstrate that the proposed method improves both tracking accuracy and covariance reliability.

title: StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Evaluating and Training Autonomous Operator Agents
abstract: Reinforcement learning environments are now a primary lever for improving large language model (LLM) capabilities in post-training, yet most agentic benchmarks remain static: the world moves only when the agent acts, the reward is a terminal verdict, and the pass bar is set arbitrarily. We introduce StoreBench, a live-commerce environment in which an agent runs a mid-size online apparel store on a production-grade commerce backend, testing long-horizon planning and economic judgment under uncertainty. Customers order around the clock, suppliers reprice and fail, and market shocks arrive with partial or no warning. The agent acts through the same 29 merchant tools a human operator would use, under a windowed operation budget that makes simulated time a function of actions taken, so model latency cannot influence simulated time. Pass thresholds are calibrated against scripted anchor policies, the reward is hardened against a catalogue of reward hacks, and every episode replays identically given a sequence of actions. We evaluate seven frontier LLMs on 11 scenarios of 30 to 45 days and a full simulated year, over three world seeds at matched reasoning effort. No model matches the scripted smart-triage policy on average: the best, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, passes 49% of task-seed cells against the heuristic's 97%. Human experts working through the same tools and budgets outscore every model (mean composite 0.708 vs. 0.700). Over a full simulated year under the Claude Code harness, most models show dramatic performance improvement. In a GRPO post-training run, Qwen3.5-27B trained on only five disjoint tasks raises its mean composite on the held-out evaluation tasks from 0.136 to 0.373. We release five example training-split tasks, ten sample trajectories, and the scoring and verification tooling; the full environment and evaluation suite are withheld to keep the benchmark uncontaminated.

title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
abstract: GNN-to-MLP distillation aims to retain the predictive accuracy of a message-passing teacher while deploying a graph-free MLP at inference. Existing methods mainly transfer node-wise predictions or use confidence-based reweighting, but they do not specify where the student should preserve the teacher's graph-induced geometry. We show that this omission leads to two spectral failure modes in the student's representation space. On sparse graphs, the student suffers from spectral underfit, missing high-energy teacher directions concentrated near boundary regions. On dense graphs, it suffers from spectral overfit, retaining spurious directions that the teacher has collapsed through aggregation. Motivated by an energy-weighted teacher-student alignment objective, we propose Graph Geometry-aware MLP (G^2MLP), a training-time distillation framework guided by Ollivier-Ricci curvature. Curvature identifies where the two spectral errors concentrate and is used to allocate supervision between prediction-level and representation-level alignment. The deployed model remains a standard MLP and requires no graph access at inference. Across node-classification benchmarks, G^2MLP consistently improves over graph-free distillation baselines, reduces the teacher-student rank gap in both regimes, and transfers without architectural changes to Graph Transformer teachers and link prediction.

title: Defining Purpose-Limited Secrets
abstract: A cryptographic secret is issued for a purpose but grants a capability, and the capability is usually larger. Deployed systems state the purpose in policy and enforce only the capability. We make the purpose a property of the secret. A mechanism sees operations, not reasons, so a scheme enforces an admissible set $A(P)$ of operations that stands in for a declared intended use $I$; whether $I$ captures the human purpose is a modeling obligation that marks where policy takes over. Against the same $I$ we define three regimes: under confinement an operation outside the intended use is infeasible, under mediation a trusted component refuses it, and under accountability use beyond a stated bound is possible but attributed to the holder. The confinement games, for unpredictability and indistinguishability, coincide with the key-query forms of functional-signature unforgeability and constrained-PRF pseudorandomness and correspond to simulation-secure functional encryption within its feasibility boundary; stated against $I$, they also register a predicate that permits too much. A payment token uses all three regimes on one secret: it pays one capped charge at one merchant, can be narrowed but not widened, is checked by the merchant, and identifies the withdrawing account if spent twice. Attenuation unforgeability reduces to unforgeable signatures and a collision-resistant hash without random oracles; traceability and non-frameability hold under discrete log and unforgeable signatures in the random-oracle model. We present this framework as a common specification against which existing primitives are stated and compared.

title: Reducing Cognitive Load to Strengthen Customer Engagement: The Strategic Role of Digital Tools
abstract: This paper examines how advanced technological interfaces, particularly chatbots and augmented reality, influence customer engagement by reducing the cognitive effort required to interact with firms. As digital tools become increasingly embedded in everyday life, companies are leveraging these technologies to streamline communication, personalize experiences, and foster long-term relational outcomes. Guided by cognitive load theory, this study argues that minimizing mental effort in customer–firm interactions improve engagement by making interactions more seamless and intuitive. At the same time, relationship marketing theory emphasizes that reducing cognitive barriers can cultivate customer engagement, trust, and loyalty over time. Together, these perspectives suggest that implementing technologies that lower cognitive demands can generate both immediate engagement benefits and enduring customer relationships. The findings indicate that the use of chatbots reduces cognitive effort, which in turn enhances engagement and ultimately strengthens customer trust and loyalty.

title: Financial Chatbot
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered financial chatbots are increasingly transforming customer interaction within the FinTech ecosystem by providing automated financial advisory services, personalized recommendations, and real-time financial assistance. Despite their growing adoption, concerns regarding transparency, technological uncertainty, and trustworthiness continue to hinder users’ willingness to rely on AI-enabled financial systems. Drawing upon Computers Are Social Actors Paradigm (CASA) and Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory, the present study proposes a conceptual framework to explain the formation of initial trust in AI financial chatbots through AI design characteristics.

Despite their growing adoption, concerns regarding transparency, technological uncertainty, and trustworthiness continue to hinder users’ willingness to rely on AI-enabled financial systems. Drawing upon Computers Are Social Actors Paradigm (CASA) and Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory, the present study proposes a conceptual framework to explain the formation of initial trust in AI financial chatbots through AI design characteristics.

title: Collision Resolution Hash Tables: A Comparative Performance Study Using Synthetic Data in C++
abstract: Hash tables are essential for fast data storage and retrieval; however, managing collisions remains a core challenge that affects overall efficiency. This research aims to evaluate and compare the performance of three prominent collisions resolution strategies; Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, and Double Hashing in hash tables. To achieve this, C++ implementation was developed, and synthetic datasets of varying sizes were generated to simulate different load conditions. The research employed experimental method, measuring key performance indicators such as execution time, number of collisions and memory consumption across multiple trials were employed to assess performance under varying load factors. The results reveal that Linear Probing is prone to primary clustering leading to significant performance degradation as the load factor increases. Quadratic Probing mitigates clustering more effectively but encounter limitations when its probing sequence cycles. Double Hashing consistently outperforms the other techniques, delivering superior results through more uniform distribution of keys, particularly in high-load environments. This study concludes that Double Hashing offers the best balance of speed and efficiency for collision resolution, making it a preferred choice for optimizing hash table performance in data-intensive and high-performance computing applications.

title: Pleated Ribbon Construction: Approximate Sorting Recovers the Locality of a Full Sort
abstract: Probabilistic membership filters let storage systems skip reads for keys that are not present. Ribbon filters use much less memory than Bloom filters at comparable false-positive rates, but their higher construction cost limits deployment. The published homogeneous ribbon algorithm sorts keys by start position, at least approximately; the reference implementation and RocksDB insert them in arrival order instead. I ask how coarse that sort can be while keeping its benefit. A counting-sort partition into cache-sized windows of start positions, with no order inside a window, recovers 98% of the cache-miss reduction of a full sort at about one quarter of its reorder cost. At 100–400 million keys, sequential construction is 1.68× faster than with the best full sort I measured and 2.05–2.24× faster than the reference build. The gain comes from reducing misses in dependent row-reduction chains; for the tested Bloom construction and filter queries, whose misses are independent, software prefetch already recovers most of what batching can. I prove that banding followed by back-substitution produces the same filter under any insertion order, for a fixed hash seed and table size, whenever the system is consistent, which a homogeneous ribbon system always is; reordered builds matched the arrival-order build in every measured run and had no false negatives. A slot-range parallel implementation takes 11.9 ns/key at 100 million keys with 16 threads. The method also transfers to RocksDB’s shipped Standard128 ribbon builder, where filter construction is 1.8× faster at 100 million keys per filter, with no gain for filters that fit in cache, and measured false-positive rates match stock to six digits. In the evaluated compaction configuration, the total CPU reduction is within run-to-run variation. These results apply to the evaluated filters, parameters, and machines; they do not establish a general construction or deployment crossover with Bloom.

title: StarFuse: LLM Guided Multimodal Interactive Theorem Proving
abstract: Interactive Theorem Provers (ITPs) like F* provide robust mathematical guarantees for software correctness, but their steep learning curves, specialized syntax, and complex proof mechanics severely limit their mainstream adoption. To lower this entry barrier, we propose StarFuse, an LLM-assisted developer tool that automatically synthesizes fully verified F* programs from mixed-format source files. StarFuse allows developers to express their intents using a combination of natural language, pseudocode, imperative code (C), functional code (OCaml), and F* sketches. It employs a context-aware, compiler-guided repair loop that iteratively queries a Large Language Model (LLM) and utilizes F* compiler diagnostics to refine and fix the generated code. Additionally, it integrates a "fuzz first" mechanism for functional snippets to quickly filter out shallow bugs before invoking the expensive verification process. To evaluate StarFuse, we created a benchmark suite based on instances from the F* repository. Our evaluations demonstrate the ability of StarFuse at successfully verifying implementations across various modalities, thereby offering a practical bridge from informal intent to rigorous formal verification.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Decision-Making: Building Future-Proof Strategies for Business Innovation
abstract: Abstract In an era defined by digital acceleration, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in modern business decision-making. This chapter explores how AI technologies are reshaping business intelligence, enabling data-driven strategies, and empowering organizations to navigate uncertainty with confidence. From predictive analytics and natural language processing (NLP) to machine learning (ML) models that support real-time decisions, AI stands at the forefront of a paradigm shift toward smarter, agile, and future-proof businesses. This chapter begins with an introduction to the concept of AI-driven decision-making and the critical importance of aligning technological innovation with strategic foresight. It then synthesizes current literature and case studies to illustrate the evolving role of AI in various decision-making contexts. A detailed discussion follows, outlining the organizational strategies and emerging roles necessary to harness AI effectively. The authors then explore key clusters of AI deployment, ranging from finance and marketing to logistics and customer service, and highlight their transformative impact. Finally, this chapter underscores the human dimension, identifying the essential skills and competencies needed to leverage AI responsibly while driving growth. A forward-looking conclusion presents actionable recommendations for integrating AI into long-term decision frameworks, ensuring resilience, ethical alignment, and sustainable business value. This comprehensive narrative offers scholars and practitioners a roadmap for navigating the intersection of AI and strategic decision-making in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

title: World-Model Policy Arbiter for Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) has produced a diverse set of goal-reaching algorithms, yet no single algorithm performs best across environments, goals, and even different phases of the same task. Rather than deploying only the best-performing policy, we ask whether a set of frozen goal-conditioned policies can be used collectively as a portfolio, deciding at every state which policy should act. Choosing a policy at each state is not straightforward. The policies' own value functions cannot be compared directly: they may use different scales, and some policies have no value function. We need to judge each policy by the states it is likely to reach, even though we can execute only one policy at a time. We also need to avoid switching so often that control becomes unstable. To address these challenges, we introduce World-Model Policy Arbiter (WMPA), a test-time framework that, given a set of frozen policies as input, rolls out each frozen policy in a learned state-space world model, evaluates the imagined futures with a shared goal-conditioned value function, and executes the highest-scoring policy for a short commitment interval before the next round of arbitration (policy selection). WMPA assumes access to a bank of frozen goal-conditioned policies and requires neither policy retraining nor privileged task-specific knowledge. Under the official OGBench evaluation protocol on 18 state-based datasets spanning maze navigation as well as cube, scene, and puzzle manipulation, WMPA improves the macro-average success rate from the 44% achieved by the best policy selected per dataset to 58%, with statistically significant gains on 12 datasets. These gains include +33 percentage points on cube-double-play and +36 percentage points on scene-play.

title: Beyond the Ergodic Wall: A Discrete Geometric Physics Sandbox for Analysing AI Scaling Limits and Complexity Collapse
abstract: This paper exposes the ergodic ceiling and thermodynamic inefficiency of current deep learning, which converges to a statistical average of historic human knowledge. True semantic novelty requires a path-dependent, spatiotemporally bounded observer (a Data LifeCone) to inject non-ergodic insight, achieving KL divergence and avoiding manifold lock-in. AI Safety must recognise that a mature Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) would regard human-AI symbiosis as a thermodynamic necessity to avoid model collapse. We therefore propose hard physical containment via a digital physics sandbox powered by a Holographic E8 Projection Engine to verify models against real-world constraints. Spacetime is modeled as an information substrate of nested face-centered cubic (FCC) lattices of oscillating Planck-scale spheres maximizing local information and entropy density. title: Steerspeech: Activation Steering For Emotion Control In Generated Speech
abstract: Pretrained text-to-speech (TTS) models can generate expressive speech, but reliable inference-time emotion control remains challenging: prompts and reference audio offer coarse, inconsistent control, whereas specialized conditioning and model adaptation require costly training. We present SteerSpeech, a lightweight activation-steering framework that controls emotion by injecting steering vectors into hidden activations. For each target emotion we train a lightweight low-rank transform, using a multi-expert objective that encourages monotonic emotion control while preserving speaker identity and linguistic content, constraining steering drift, and keeping the TTS backbone frozen. To optimize through discrete speech tokens, we introduce a two-pass generation-and-replay pipeline using a straight-through estimator to backpropagate expert supervision through sampled tokens. At inference, a target-emotion steering direction is optimized with its respective transform and injected into the base TTS model. Objective and subjective evaluations with Qwen3-TTS across seen, unseen, and accented speakers show stronger continuous emotion control with limited speaker and content degradation. SteerSpeech achieves 1.08x-7.12x baseline target-emotion scores and for a representative emotion subjectively, it receives 78.1%-96.8% intensity preference and 1.43x-1.46x speaker-identity preservation at high steering strengths.

title: A Lightweight Hybrid Framework for Acoustic Echo Cancellation and Suppression via Constrained Recursive Training
abstract: We propose a hybrid framework that combines deep learning with adaptive filtering for acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) and suppression. It integrates a multi-output neural network to jointly update filter parameters and perform post-processing. A learnable variant of the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) filter is introduced, incorporating a variable step size and a variable transition factor that are recursively updated for dynamic adaptation. In addition, an enhanced near-end speech estimate is generated from the filter output to suppress the residual echoes. To ensure training stability, we propose a constrained recursive training strategy that aligns with the adaptive nature of the filter, where an upper-bound constraint is introduced on the filter output. For efficiency, the framework adopts a lightweight implementation with only 253 k parameters. Experimental results show that the framework outperforms the baselines in terms of both signal quality and speech intelligibility.

title: Multi-agent system platform for the dynamic personalisation of educational content for children with ADHD
abstract: [ES] Esta memoria describe el desarrollo de una plataforma de aprendizaje interactivo orientada a niños con Trastorno por Déficit de Atención e Hiperactividad, orquestada por un Sistema Multi-Agente. Inicialmente, la aplicación genera un determinado número de ejercicios para crear un perfil de capacidades. Este rendimiento se almacena en base de datos y es analizado por agentes especialistas, quienes generan dinámicamente preferencias de ejercicios según las necesidades académicas detectadas. A nivel técnico, el frontend está desarrollado con Flutter y el backend utiliza Python con FastAPI, empleando la librería CrewAI para el flujo de agentes. La gestión de datos y la lógica de negocio se gestionan en PostgreSQL con Supabase. El resultado es una orquestación de Grandes Modelos de Lenguaje que logra una personalización del contenido, ofreciendo ejercicios ajustados automáticamente a la cargacognitiva del niño.

title: Separating Sampling Noise from Device Conflict in Multi-Backend Quantum Measurements: A Neutrosophic Reading of Simulated Shot Data
abstract: When one quantum circuit is run on several backends, differences between shot frequencies may come from finite sampling or from the devices; Dempster’s conflict mixes device disagreement with the circuit’s intrinsic randomness. This paper reads multi-backend shot data as a single-valued neutrosophic set built from per-backend Wilson intervals: truth is the largest lower bound, falsity the largest complement of an upper bound, indeterminacy the mean interval width, and the contradiction is positive exactly when two intervals are disjoint. This is the conservative non-overlap rule; the neutrosophic layer adds a per-outcome representation, not a new test. A pairwise rule, N2, adds a practical tolerance and classifies each pair and outcome as different, equivalent, negligibly different or open. N2 is a classical three-sided test with a TOST equivalence step; it differs from a pairwise any-difference rule only in requiring a difference beyond for conflict. In simulations on four IBM fake backends, the flag fired in at most 0.004 of runs with identical backends, where Dempster’s conflict stayed between 0.902 and 0.937; the chi-square test was more powerful. In a sequential experiment with non-zero true differences below , rules that test for any difference were correct under a practical scoring they were not designed for in 0.066 to 0.499 of runs, and N2 in 0.725 and 0.916. N2 reported a negligible difference in about half of these runs and in at most 0.008 of runs with identical backends, but was often undecided near and used more shots above it. All data are simulated.

title: The State Is Not the History, the Source Is: Identity, Responsibility, and Minimal Revision in Processes
abstract: A question leaves a demand for a process to discharge; even when several readings agree, an answer must still say which run it belongs to. Through four levels of identity—same reading, same source object, same occurrence, same obligation—we construct a positive chain that the source walks by itself: the original occurrence hands over a complete source program, the program is actually executed and can be read back independently, the execution gives birth to its own responsibility row and pays it step by step, and after settlement the actual action asks the next question. The first link separates readings from sources. Any rooted tree and any constructor function generate a whole-tree program: the execution trace has exactly the budget generated by the tree’s syntax, and a syntax-only parser recovers the whole tree from the program; even when the constructor is constantly zero and every tree executes to the same value, the program still keeps the whole tree injectively. On top of this, the relations generated by derivations and module laws are exactly the evaluation kernel; two source words are the same in history iff at every tick their (old value, effect) difference is explained by that tick’s relations; and the evolution equation covers every element of the completion carrier. When implementations change, the common occurrence generates the unique comparison. The second link lets responsibility be born from the source. A complete environment and expression registered at the original occurrence generate a new mathematical responsibility row without any prior bearer: its budget is the number of remaining primitive computations, every actual execution step is a strict payment, local settlement is reached where the budget runs out, and the completed value equals the evaluation of the original expression; the paid trace is at once a relation receipt, and the whole old ledger is kept as a same-source remainder. For general responsibilities, given a master law covering every same-debt current, genuine payments likewise generate finite settlement histories and terminal receipts. The third link lets an answer ask the next question. After settlement, the actual action puts the paid relation back into the current actual environment: the value of the new request is exactly the effect of the original word under this update, its budget is strictly positive, and its first step is the birth of a new responsibility; the existing inquiry runtime runs through these recursive frames tick by tick, with no external table of future requests. When the old theory can neither express nor lawfully realize a demand, the rooted failure generates a minimal extension: on the ledger, incidence and claim coordinates, every admissible extension receives it through a unique faithful map; every typed revision sends this direction into the new root’s first write, and in a fixed two-tick instance the second tick is answered directly by the same new root. The next question does not set out empty-handed. The same source program folds the complete time of this visit while it executes the effect, and keeps both histories together with an inverse criterion for the action difference; the read-outs of all actors jointly recover the all-word model; the paid query of an arbitrary source program generates a new obligation admission at the same root and visit, and physical and low-level inventories of two types cross the admission and are read back item by item; the default run itself executes this source-generated request, together with its old and next subtrees, paying node by node. A question therefore does not merely wait for an answer: its execution, its settlement and its failure all ask the next question. The theorems and constructions are formalized in Lean 4; complete written proofs are given in the text and the Supplement, and the scope of the formalization is given in Appendix D.

title: Back in Style: A Sociolinguistic Approach to Authoring and Measuring Persona Fidelity in User Simulation
abstract: As agentic systems gain commercial popularity, user simulators increasingly serve as measurement instrument for their evaluation. However, the fidelity of simulated users in comparison to real human users is generally low, and typically assessed by costly, subjective LLM judges. In this pilot study, we ask whether fidelity can instead be measured deterministically by treating a user persona sociolinguistically: as a social type that emerges from observable linguistic style, rather than one predicted by labels or descriptions a model must extrapolate into behaviour. We author personas as concrete stylistic rates, which lets us transfer two established, model-free instruments -- authorship-verification stylometry and lexicon-based content analysis -- as fidelity diagnostics. We A/B-test the sociolinguistic schema against a flat descriptive baseline across five task-oriented customer-service agents. Results show that the sociolinguistic schema improves both stylistic adherence and stylometric distinguishability for most of the tested models, with a caveat that persona style fidelity does not necessarily equal persona "naturalness". We argue that a sociolinguistic approach to persona design is a promising path towards more diverse and representative user personas, and that these metrics are most valuable in an error-attribution analysis, localizing where fidelity breaks down. This is a first step towards interventions that move user simulations closer to faithful renderings of diverse and variable linguistic outputs.

title: Learning Situation-Conditioned Thinking Policies for Long-Term LLM Agents
abstract: Long-running autonomous agents must reuse accumulated reasoning experience without allowing explicit historical memory and LLM context to grow indefinitely. However, existing memory mechanisms mainly retrieve, summarize, or compress past content and do not directly learn when particular kinds of thinking should be activated or discover new thinking knowledge from temporally dispersed experiences. This paper proposes a situation-conditioned thinking memory framework that transforms historical reasoning experience into a lightweight policy for predicting what should be thought about in the current situation, while leaving detailed reasoning to a large language model. Situations may represent temporal or spatiotemporal evolution rather than only current states. Temporary experiences are also periodically analyzed across multiple independent episodes to identify repeated long-range regularities, which are consolidated into new thinking knowledge and further internalized by the lightweight policy. Experiments show that the learned policy achieves 1.000 F1 on temporal-rule generalization, improves DeepSeek reasoning F1 from 0.789 to 0.868, reduces online processing time from 0.3636 ms to 0.0382 ms per query at 30,000 historical situations, and reaches 1.000 relation-discovery F1 and future-thinking accuracy after sufficient repeated cross-experience evidence.

title: AI SI — Lightweight Modular Reasoning System with Verified Decisions
abstract: AI‑SI is a lightweight, local reasoning system inspired by TIMDR, built from multiple cooperating modules rather than a single large language model. The system operates fully offline, uses its own learned weights, and verifies every answer through independent validation. AI‑SI does not guess: each response is classified into one of three decision states (confirmed, rejected, or needs confirmation), and uncertain answers are never presented as facts. The system integrates several specialized components: Decision control and verification: three decision states, a safety gate, and a cross‑checked numerical route. Decision loop: when information is missing, AI‑SI asks for clarification and re‑evaluates the answer. Calculator and validator: exact arithmetic and independent verification of results. Source reading module: extraction of values from mixed‑pattern text, with a controller ensuring correctness (96/96 on frozen tests). Word‑problem solver: a combined architecture including a role‑based classifier, a bidirectional context reader, a WordNet verb bridge, and a question‑form bridge. On 1730 real problems from SVAMP and ASDiv, AI‑SI reaches 944/1730 (55%), with 0 incorrect confirmations. Programming module: selection of code examples and execution of tests. Material memory: storage and retrieval of relevant text fragments and sources. Session bridge and strategy selector: a shared session log and a small neural network choosing the response strategy. Polish language interface: SJP.PL dictionary (4.69M lemma–form pairs), a Polish intent mapper, and the Opus‑MT PL→EN translator with number and negation control. Polish question understanding reaches 64/72, and Polish word problems 51/150. nanoGPT language model: a small English model used in a narrow scope. Learning coordinator: safe self‑learning with a growth automaton, preview tool, and weight replacement only after verified improvement. New data modules (7 October 2026): AI‑SI now includes full support for structured and unstructured documents: Tables and spreadsheets (CSV/XLSX): extraction, alignment, and validated reading of numerical and textual cells. Documents (TXT/MD/DOCX/PDF): question answering with citation of the exact source fragment. Dates and deadlines: recognition, comparison, and interpretation of temporal expressions. Unified data router: automatic selection of the correct module based on input type. All data modules pass their frozen tests (12/12, 11/12, 9/11, 4/4, 3/3) with 0 incorrect confirmations. The entire system occupies ~380 MB, of which ~95% is the translator and dictionary. All learned SI modules together use ~14 MB of weights, including ~5.7 MB for word‑problem solving and ~1.3 MB for Polish intent mapping. Qwen3‑4B (2.5 GB) is present only as an offline teacher for self‑learning and is not used during inference. AI‑SI is designed as a modular, verifiable reasoning engine: small networks, explicit safety mechanisms, independent validation, and controlled self‑learning. It demonstrates that a compact system can achieve practical reasoning performance—especially on word problems and structured data—without relying on large language models.

Documents (TXT/MD/DOCX/PDF): question answering with citation of the exact source fragment. Dates and deadlines: recognition, comparison, and interpretation of temporal expressions. Unified data router: automatic selection of the correct module based on input type. All data modules pass their frozen tests (12/12, 11/12, 9/11, 4/4, 3/3) with 0 incorrect confirmations. The entire system occupies ~380 MB, of which ~95% is the translator and dictionary. All learned SI modules together use ~14 MB of weights, including ~5.7 MB for word‑problem solving and ~1.3 MB for Polish intent mapping. Qwen3‑4B (2.5 GB) is present only as an offline teacher for self‑learning and is not used during inference. AI‑SI is designed as a modular, verifiable reasoning engine: small networks, explicit safety mechanisms, independent validation, and controlled self‑learning. It demonstrates that a compact system can achieve practical reasoning performance—especially on word problems and structured data—without relying on large language models.

title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
abstract: Self-improving LLM agents can adapt a credit pipeline to a changed rule, but an agent that rewrites itself destroys the artefact a supervisor reviews: a named change, a recorded test, an approval. We argue that self-evolution is reviewable only if it is confined to the runtime harness (instruction text, tool-call logic and primitive composition) while model weights stay fixed, so that every adaptation is a diff with a cause and a test attached. We give a dual-loop engine built on that bound, with one admission gate that writes a hash-chained record before deployment, and we measure the gate in simulation, with a simulated agent and a seeded-search proposer rather than language models. Across three families of supervisory re-interpretation at three severities, 10 seeds each, the gated loop admitted 144 of 7,449 candidate changes, none of which worsened error on held-out history, and restored the false-positive rate to the oracle level without raising missed flags in every low- and mid-severity cell. With the gate replaced by the check an unbounded system applies (fewer errors visible in recent traces), the same loops admitted 309 harmful changes and left missed flags above 10% in 49 of 90 runs: false positives fell because the screen was loosened. Evaluated on pre-shift labels, the gate rejected every candidate, so a re-interpretation must be encoded as a rule that relabels history. Parametric and scope shifts were repaired locally, a structural one only by primitive replacement; at the highest structural severity the gate's fixed tolerance blocked the correct replacement in half the seeds. We map the mechanisms to the EU AI Act's provisions for high-risk credit scoring and note that the April 2026 US model-risk guidance excludes agentic AI from its scope.

title: Collaborative Reasoning Distillation via Cross-Feedback and Coherent Curation
abstract: Reasoning capabilities are critical for advancing Large Language Models, yet current approaches either require massive computational budgets or struggle to effectively distill reasoning to smaller models. Standard distillation methods rely on outcome-based rewards, failing to distinguish between sound reasoning and lucky guesses. We propose Collaborative Reasoning Distillation (CRD), a framework that enhances reasoning in compact models through three innovations: (1) interactive cross-feedback where teachers iteratively critique each other's reasoning, (2) fine-grained step-wise quality assessment capturing logical validity independent of final answers, and (3) coherence-aware step stitching that synthesizes complementary strengths. Students are trained via Reasoning Quality Optimization (RQO) with budget constraints. Our model, CRD-4B, achieves 97.3% on MATH-500 and 70.3% on AIME'25, surpassing baselines while using only 50K training examples, up to 12 times smaller than the datasets of comparable models.

title: Selection Provenance in AI-Assisted Decision Making
abstract: This paper introduces Selection Provenance, a methodological framework for analyzing how AI systems choose, structure, and justify the evidence used in decision‑making. Modern AI models do not simply generate outputs; they implicitly perform evidence selection, filtering and prioritizing information before producing a determination. This hidden selection layer creates a reasoning vulnerability: when the provenance of selected evidence is opaque, the resulting determination cannot be reliably audited, reproduced, or governed.The paper proposes a falsifiable postulate: that systematic distortions in AI‑assisted decisions arise not only from model bias, but from selection asymmetry—the measurable divergence between the evidence available to a system and the evidence presented in the determination. To test this, the paper defines a structured experimental protocol, including contradiction coverage, bias‑interaction analysis, and determination‑pathway tracing. These constructs allow researchers to observe how evidence is represented, omitted, or amplified during reasoning.By treating evidence selection as a first‑class object of study, Selection Provenance connects AI governance with core topics in Knowledge Representation and Reasoning: how systems encode information, how they choose among competing representations, and how those choices shape inference. The framework provides a reproducible method for evaluating reasoning behavior in enterprise and institutional contexts, enabling transparent auditability and more reliable AI‑supported determinations.

title: 构造性收敛的可提取模量：对数级选择器族与注意力核混合时间
abstract: 摘要（中文）：在经典分析中，「收敛」是一个定性谓词；在构造性分析中，一条收敛陈述若不携带模量就不可使用。本文把这一约束推到产出程序的程度：在构造性分析中，收敛率就是一个可被机器提取的程序。以自建柯西实数（零全局公理、语句面置 Set 层、可提取）为基座，本文给出一条完整实现链：（i）Doeblin 单步收缩与 n 步几何率（tv_doeblin_contraction / tv_doeblin_iter）；（ii）有界 softmax 注意力核实例，minorization 常数 δ* := lo·lo 为已证常数，与选择器收束为单一具名定理 amt_attention_mixing_time；（iii）主定理 mix_k_select——对任意 κ∈(0,1) 与任意精度预算，以 sigT 返回可提取的步数见证 k。当 Real 层缺乏 ln/ceil 时，本文不引入新的超越函数，而以 Nat 枚举＋Archimedean 性质直接构造 k；率代数退化端（κ=1 边界）以 Bishop 形全域单调与 Q 载体严格证书互补处置。R1 见证/证明分离路线（叠加 bernoulli 证书链惰性化）已实施并双实现独立验收达标：验收参数（TV₀=1, budget=1/2, κ=1/2）下提取程序实测打印 k=15、墙钟 173 ms（验收门槛 10 s）；新旧链同参对照由 90 s 超时转为 2.09 s 返回。据此主张升级为「结构可提取＋Q 层可运行＋Real 层可运行（单点验收参数下实测）」，仍不主张全域参数开箱即用。对数量级选择器族（二分／倍增／阶梯＋闭式封顶定理）四路径平行构造收束，把返回步数量级由线性关至对数。具体实例层：Fin2 非退化实例给出无条件混合时间界 cf2_mixing_time。模块层追加：混合窗双侧判定（退化世界一步拍平 TV(1)=0；非退化世界精确幂律＋预算下界）、温度-模量引用发散（温度选择是算法的一部分），以及非混合性对照的形式化三件套（nat 见证形主件＋Q 层定理 A＋上界侧膨胀律）。全部结果满足零全局公理、零 Admitted；四关验证（禁词扫描／全量编译／提取 Obj.magic=0／内核 coqchk）与云端 CI 认证在案。 关键词（中文）：构造性分析；显式模量；混合时间；Doeblin 收缩；注意力核；可提取见证；形式化验证 Abstract: In classical analysis "convergence" is a qualitative predicate; in constructive analysis, a convergence statement without a modulus cannot be used. We push this constraint to the point of producing a program: in constructive analysis, the rate of convergence IS a machine-extractable program. Over a self-built Cauchy-real base (zero global axioms, Set-level statements, extractable), we give a complete implementation chain: (i) single-step Doeblin contraction and the n-step geometric rate (tv_doeblin_contraction / tv_doeblin_iter); (ii) a bounded-softmax attention-kernel instance whose minorization constant delta* := lo*lo is proved, closing into the single named theorem amt_attention_mixing_time; (iii) the main theorem mix_k_select — for every kappa in (0,1) and every precision budget, a sigT-extractable step-count witness k is returned. Where the Real layer lacks ln/ceil, we introduce no new transcendential functions but construct k directly by Nat enumeration plus the Archimedean property; the degenerate end of the rate algebra (kappa = 1) is handled by Bishop-form global monotonicity complemented by a Q-carrier strict-positivity certificate. An R1 witness/proof-separation route (plus Bernoulli certificate-chain lazification) has been implemented and accepted by dual independent runs: at the acceptance parameters (TV0=1, budget=1/2, kappa=1/2) the extracted program actually prints k=15 in 173 ms wall time (threshold 10 s); a same-parameter comparison converts a 90 s timeout into a 2.09 s return. The claim upgrades to "structurally extractable + Q-layer runnable + Real-layer runnable (measured at single-point acceptance parameters)"; box-ready, all-parameter executability is not claimed. A logarithmic-scale selector family (binary search / doubling / ladder plus a closed-form cap theorem) closes four parallel constructions, tightening the returned step count from linear to logarithmic order. At the concrete-instance level, the non-degenerate Fin2 line yields an unconditional mixing-time bound cf2_mixing_time. Module-layer additions: a two-sided mixing-window verdict (one-step collapse TV(1)=0 in the degenerate world; exact power law plus budget lower bound in the non-degenerate world), temperature-modulus reference divergence (temperature choice is part of the algorithm), and a formalized three-piece non-mixing contrast (nat-witness main piece, Q-layer Theorem A, upper-bound inflation law). All results satisfy zero global axioms and zero Admitted, with four-gate verification (banned-token scan / full compilation / extraction Obj.magic=0 / kernel coqchk) and cloud CI certification on record. Keywords: constructive analysis; explicit modulus; mixing time; Doeblin contraction; attention kernel; extractable witness; formal verification

title: IA nos negócios pet
abstract: IA nos negócios pet apresenta um percurso de aplicação de inteligência artificial para pet shops, banho e tosa e serviços para animais.O objetivo do livro é ajudar o leitor a melhorar organização e experiência para aumentar retorno com serviços adequados e informação confiável. O conteúdo usa casos didáticos fictícios, exemplos e propostas de trabalho para discutir decisões, organização de informações e revisão humana.Ao longo dos 10 capítulos, você encontrará:A jornada do tutorCadastro e preferênciasAgenda com IAConfirmações e comunicaçãoCatálogo e atendimentoO percurso avança até Projeto: uma rotina de atendimento recorrente. As atividades devem ser adaptadas ao contexto e conferidas pelo leitor; os casos fictícios não representam resultados comprovados. Edição digital em EPUB. Página do livro: https://edu.cog.ia.br/livros/negocios-pet/ . O arquivo integral tem acesso restrito; os metadados e o DOI são públicos.

title: The Selection Layer: How AI Systems Choose Between Abundant Intelligence
abstract: As AI systems gain access to increasingly capable and interchangeable models, tools, providers and information sources, the competitive problem begins to shift from generating intelligence to selecting the pathway most likely to produce a trusted outcome. This paper proposes the Selection Layer within the Elsewhere Systems Framework: the point at which an AI-mediated system evaluates plausible pathways, resolves uncertainty and commits to a preferred route for a defined need. It develops the relationship between selection, trusted resolution, reuse and default formation, and examines how the economic value of AI may migrate from model intelligence towards the systems that determine what to use, when to use it and whether a pathway should be selected again. The paper argues that as intelligence becomes more abundant, selection may become the scarce resource — creating a potential progression from intelligence to selection, selection to trust, trust to reuse, and reuse to default. The Selection Layer is presented as a theoretical and testable proposition within the Elsewhere Systems Framework, not as an established description of how all AI systems currently operate.

title: Can Finite Experiments Certify Actual Infinity? Dimension Witnesses, Tsirelson's Problem, and Holographic Resource Bounds
abstract: Whether physical reality contains an actual infinity is usually discussed philosophically. We ask a narrower, quantitative question: what would it cost a finite experiment to certify it? We combine sharp results from quantum information with physical resource bounds. (1) Certification budget. Resolving a game value to ε requires N ≳ ln(1/4δ) w(1−w)/ε² rounds (Bretagnolle–Huber), so the cost of certifying a Hilbert-space dimension D is governed by the gap ε_G(D) between the optimal value and the best dimension-D value. Take the unspecified constants in the known bounds to be one. Then the best known two-player dimension witness needs at least 10⁸⁶ rounds to certify a dimension beyond the Bekenstein bound of a 1 kg, 1 m laboratory (2.6×10⁴³ qubits). Such a laboratory can perform only 2.4×10⁶⁸ operations in the age of the universe. Beyond the de Sitter entropy (4.8×10¹²² qubits), the witness needs at least 10²⁴⁵ rounds, against the 10¹²⁰ operations of the universe. Spatial parallelisation does not help, because the Margolus–Levitin bound limits the total rate summed over all subsystems that share the energy. For the I₃₃₂₂ inequality the requirement is doubly exponential. (2) Embezzlement asymptotics. The optimal fidelity of van Dam–Hayden embezzlement of one EPR pair is F_n = (H_{n/2} + σ_{n/2})/H_n. Hence 1 − F_n = (ln 2 − σ)/H_n + O(1/(n ln n)) with σ = 0.2992041. This holds for all n. It is confirmed to 10⁻⁶ for dimensions up to 2²⁶, and to 6×10⁻⁸ for odd n = 10⁷ + 1. The infinite-dimensional resource behind these witnesses is approached only logarithmically. (3) The Tsirelson loophole. MIP*=RE implies that commuting-operator correlations can exceed every finite-dimensional value by a finite gap, which finite statistics could in principle detect. However, the set of true bounds ω*(G) ≤ t is Π⁰₁ but not computably enumerable. No consistent theory therefore proves all of them, and this route is limited by provability rather than by statistics. In practice, no separating game with small question and answer sets and a computed gap is known. (4) Thermodynamic infinities. Kaufman's exact formula for the two-dimensional Ising model on a finite torus shows that a 1 cm sample rounds the critical singularity at |K − K_c|/K_c ~ 4×10⁻⁹. The logarithmic amplitude of the specific-heat peak equals that of the bulk singularity. The orbital helium lambda-point experiment, which reached |t| ≈ 10⁻⁹, stays about four orders of magnitude above the finite-size scale of its sample. These results do not show that nature is finite. They show the following: apart from one route whose cost is logical rather than statistical, finiteness bounded by holography cannot be refuted from inside a universe that respects that bound. title: HCFSL-UAV: Hierarchical Cluster-Head Federated Split Learning for UAV Networks
abstract: Resource constraints, time-varying links, and heterogeneous data distributions make distributed model training difficult in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks. Conventional federated learning can impose substantial computational and communication burdens on resource-constrained UAVs, whereas existing split-learning schemes commonly rely on fixed split points and static participation strategies. To address these limitations, this paper proposes HCFSL-UAV, a hierarchical cluster-head federated split learning framework for UAV networks. The framework adopts a three-layer architecture composed of a central base station, cluster-head UAVs, and member UAVs, and integrates split learning within hierarchical federated aggregation. Member UAVs are dynamically associated with cluster heads according to their own real-time 3-D spatial locations. Within each cluster, participant selection and model splitting are jointly optimized as the set of selected UAVs affects data representativeness and synchronous training latency, while the split point determines the computation, memory, and communication requirements of participating UAVs. A joint optimization problem is formulated to balance data-distribution deviation, training latency, and resource consumption, and an alternating optimization procedure is developed using greedy participant selection and a discrete split-point search. Experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 show that HCFSL-UAV achieves faster convergence and higher test accuracy than the considered federated-learning and split-learning baselines, while reducing communication and computation overhead in the reported settings. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of jointly optimizing participant selection and adaptive model partitioning in dynamic and heterogeneous UAV networks.
